title: DIFC Data Protection Regulations (as amended September 2023), including Regulation 10: Processing of Personal Data through Autonomous and Semi-Autonomous Systems
summary_short: DIFC Data Protection Regulation 10 governs AI systems that process personal data. It requires deployers and operators to give notice and provide assessments, bars commercial use unless designed to meet listed principles, and conditions high-risk processing on audit requirements and an Autonomous Systems Officer.
summary_long: The document is Regulation 10 (Processing of Personal Data through Autonomous and Semi-Autonomous Systems) of the DIFC Data Protection Regulations as amended in September 2023. Regulation 10.1.1 defines System, Deployer, Operator and Provider. Under 10.2.1, Deployers and Operators processing personal data for AI systems must adhere to the general principles in Article 9 of the Law. Under 10.2.2, where an application or website service uses such systems, Deployers or Operators must give notice on first use, describe the system's purposes, outputs and safeguards, and provide on request evidence of audit or certification compliance, human-intervention algorithms, risk and impact assessments, and a register of use cases and recipients. Under 10.3.1, systems affecting data subjects must be designed to be ethical, fair, transparent, secure and accountable. Under 10.3.2, no person may make such a system available for commercial use unless it processes personal data only for human-defined or human-approved purposes and meets 10.3.1 and any Commissioner audit requirements. Under 10.3.3, high-risk processing is permitted only if the Commissioner has set audit requirements, the system complies with them, it processes only for human-defined or human-approved purposes, and an Autonomous Systems Officer has been appointed. Under 10.3.4, Deployers are deemed controllers and Operators deemed processors. Under 10.3.5, data subjects may complain under Parts 9 and 10 of the Law. The document contains only Regulation 10. It states no penalties and no commencement date, and the Law it cross-refers to is not included.

title: Federal Decree-Law No. 45 of 2021 Concerning the Protection of Personal Data
summary_short: The decree-law regulates processing of personal data in the UAE, binding controllers and processors and granting data subjects rights, including over automated decisions. It requires consent or a listed exception, security measures, breach notification, and restricts cross-border transfers. It applies from 2 January 2022.
summary_long: The decree-law sets general rules for processing personal data by controllers and processors in the UAE, and by controllers and processors outside the UAE that process data of data subjects in the UAE. It excludes government data, government entities, data held by security and judicial bodies, personal-purpose processing, health and banking data governed by other legislation, and free-zone entities with their own data protection laws. Processing without the data subject's consent is prohibited unless an enumerated exception applies, and consent must be provable, clear and withdrawable. Processing principles include purpose limitation, data minimisation, accuracy and security. Controllers and processors must apply technical and organisational measures, keep records, notify the Office of breaches, and appoint a data protection officer in listed high-risk cases. Data subjects have rights to information, portability, rectification, erasure, restriction and objection, including to decisions based on automated processing and a right to human review. Impact assessments are required for high-risk processing. Cross-border transfers are allowed where the destination offers adequate protection or on listed grounds. Complaints go to the Office. Administrative sanctions are to be set by Cabinet decision; the text states no amounts. The decree-law applies from 2 January 2022; the executive regulation is due within six months, and controllers have six months after it is issued to comply.
text_version: Official Arabic text (original) of Federal Decree-Law No. 45 of 2021 as published on the UAE federal legislation portal

title: Decreto 105/2026 - Decreto N° 749/2024. Modificación (prórroga del plazo de adhesión al RIGI)
summary_short: Decree 105/2026 extends by one year, from 8 July 2026, the deadline to join Argentina's RIGI large-investment incentive regime and amends Decree 749/2024's implementing rules on sector definitions (including artificial intelligence in the technology sector), imports, expansions, depreciation, dividend tax rate, foreign-exchange access and procedure. In force on publication.
summary_long: Decree 105/2026, published 19 February 2026 and in force on publication, amends the implementing regulation of Argentina's RIGI large-investment incentive regime (Decree 749/2024, Annex I). Article 1 extends by one year, from 8 July 2026, the period to adhere to the RIGI. Article 2 redefines the technology sector, which now includes artificial intelligence, and the oil and gas sector, which adds new onshore developments and offshore exploration and production. Article 8 allows expansions of pre-existing non-RIGI technology projects through a new product, subject to a USD 250 million minimum investment and a product life of up to ten years. Articles 3, 4 and 13 regulate imports by RIGI suppliers and import exemptions for capital goods. Article 11 sets optional accelerated depreciation and annual useful-life declarations to the tax agency; Article 12 sets a 7% dividend rate. Article 14 lets the Central Bank condition foreign-exchange market access for RIGI projects. Articles 15 to 17 cover supplier registry withdrawal, a 30-business-day defence period and the evaluation committee. Addressees are RIGI project companies, goods and service suppliers and public authorities.

title: Decreto 749/2024 - Reglamentación del Título VII - Régimen de Incentivo para Grandes Inversiones (RIGI) - de la Ley N° 27.742
summary_short: Implements the RIGI investment-incentive regime (Law 27.742, Title VII) for single-project vehicles making large investments in listed sectors, including technology and artificial intelligence. Covers eligibility, minimum investment, admission, import and local-supplier rules, tax, FX and stability benefits, sanctions and arbitration. Binding; effective on publication.
summary_long: Decree 749/2024 approves the regulation of Title VII of Law 27.742 (arts. 164–228), the RIGI incentive regime for large investments. Eligible are single-project vehicles (VPU) carrying out one planned project in a listed sector, including technology (software, robotics, artificial intelligence), energy, mining, infrastructure, tourism, forestry, steel, and oil and gas. Projects must meet sector minimum investments in qualifying assets. Applications go to the Application Authority (Ministry of Economy), which must decide within 45 business days; the decree adds a non-distortion test, a Panel RIGI for disputes, and supplier-development duties. Imported goods are covered by supplier registration, customs-duty exemption, destination checks and penalties. Tax benefits include optional accelerated depreciation, VAT tax-credit certificates and dividend rates; FX rules govern export proceeds. Stability protects tax and customs treatment for 30 years. Sanctions, suspension, withdrawal, termination and transitional provisions complete the text. Later amendments by decrees 940/2024, 105/2026, 748/2026 and 868/2026 are reflected in the text.

title: Disposición E 60/2016 - Dirección Nacional de Protección de Datos Personales - Cláusulas contractuales tipo de transferencia internacional. Aprobación
summary_short: Approves model contractual clauses for international transfers of personal data (assignment and services) to countries without adequate legislation. Controllers whose contracts depart from the models must seek DNPDP approval within 30 days of signing. Lists countries considered adequate. Adopted 16 Nov 2016.
summary_long: Approves two model contractual clauses for international transfers of personal data, one for assignment of data (Annex I) and one for provision of services by a processor (Annex II), to be used for transfers to countries without adequate legislation under Art. 12 of Law 25.326 and its regulatory decree. Art. 2 requires controllers that use contracts differing from the models, or lacking their principles and guarantees, to submit them to the DNPDP for approval within 30 days of signature. Art. 3 lists countries considered to have adequate legislation, including EU and EEA member states, Switzerland, Guernsey, Jersey, Isle of Man, Faroe Islands, Canada (private sector only), Andorra, New Zealand, Uruguay, and Israel (automated data only). The clauses give data subjects third-party beneficiary rights, require the importer to meet security, confidentiality and data-subject request duties, allow audits by the authority, and provide for suspension and termination of transfers where obligations are breached. The text sets no penalty amounts. It is dated 16 November 2016 and was published in the Boletín Oficial on 18 November 2016.

title: Proyecto de ley: Código Nacional Electoral. Modificaciones sobre prevención de la desinformación electoral mediante la utilización de inteligencia artificial (Expte. 3728-D-2025)
summary_short: Bill amending the Código Nacional Electoral to bar AI-generated or manipulated content used to influence elections, including impersonation of candidates and false attributions, and to allow judicially ordered removal of such content. Adds prison penalties for AI-enabled electoral deception. No entry-into-force date is stated.
summary_long: The bill amends Art. 64 ter of the Código Nacional Electoral. It keeps a ban on TV and radio electoral advertising promoting candidates or parties before 35 days before the election, and limits other electoral advertising (print, public roads, internet, mobile and fixed telephony, static displays at public events) to the campaign period. The federal electoral court must order the immediate cessation of advertising that falls outside these rules. The bill prohibits using AI to generate, alter, manipulate or synthesise digital content with the deliberate aim of influencing the electoral process through five conducts: credible impersonation of real candidates and electoral figures; false attribution of statements or acts (with an exclusion for clearly artistic, fictional, satirical or hypothetical works); fake events tied to electoral figures; dissemination of AI-generated false claims about the electoral process with actual knowledge or gross negligence; and content inciting institutional violence or simulating unauthorised public functions. A saving clause protects legitimate expression and bars prior removal or censorship. The electoral enforcement authority may, by judicial order, stop the spread of altered content. With judicial authorisation, internet intermediaries may be required to suspend, delist, block or remove identified content. Art. 2 creates Art. 128 quinquies: prison from two months to two years for AI-enabled deception that induces voting in a given way or abstention, rising to two months to three years where the disseminator is a candidate or part of a deliberately planned disinformation campaign. The text states no date from which these rules apply.</parameter>

title: Ley 25.326 - Protección de los Datos Personales
summary_short: Argentina's general personal data protection statute (sanctioned 4 October 2000, partially promulgated 30 October 2000). It governs personal data in public and private databases: principles, consent, cross-border transfer limits, data subject rights, registration, a control body, sanctions and the habeas data action.
summary_long: Argentina's general personal data protection statute. Chapter I defines personal, sensitive and health data, databases, processing, controllers and data subjects, covering public and private databases. Chapter II sets principles: data quality (Art. 4), consent with listed exceptions (Art. 5), information duties (Art. 6), limits on sensitive data (Art. 7), security and confidentiality (Arts. 9-10), assignment of data (Art. 11), and prohibition of transfers to countries without adequate protection, subject to exceptions (Art. 12). Chapter III grants information, access, rectification and deletion rights (Arts. 13-19) and bars decisions based solely on automated profiling (Art. 20). Chapter IV covers registration (Arts. 21, 24), public databases (Art. 22), processing services (Art. 25), credit reporting limits (Arts. 26, 47), direct marketing (Art. 27) and a survey exemption (Art. 28). Chapter V creates a control body (Art. 29) and allows codes of conduct (Art. 30). Chapter VI sets administrative sanctions of warning, suspension, fines of 1,000 to 100,000 pesos, and closure or cancellation (Art. 31), and adds penal code offences (Art. 32). Chapter VII regulates the habeas data action (Arts. 33-43). The statute does not mention artificial intelligence.

title: Ley 26.388 - Código Penal. Modificación (delitos informáticos)
summary_short: Amends Argentina's Penal Code (Ley 26.388, promulgated 24 June 2008) to add criminal offences for computer-related conduct: unauthorized access to restricted systems and data, interception of electronic communications, computer fraud, damage to computer data and systems, and sexual representations of minors; it also defines digital signature and document terms.
summary_long: Ley 26.388 amends the Argentine Penal Code, sanctioned 4 June 2008 and promulgated 24 June 2008. Article 1 adds definitions of document, signature and private instrument that cover digital documents and digital signatures. Article 2 replaces Art. 128 on representations of minors, with prison terms for producing, distributing or possessing such material and for facilitating access to pornography for minors under fourteen. Article 3 renames the chapter on violation of secrets to cover privacy. Article 4 replaces Art. 153 on opening or intercepting electronic communications, with prison of 15 days to 6 months, up to one year if content is published, and double special disqualification for officials who abuse their functions. Article 5 adds Art. 153 bis on knowing unauthorized access to restricted computer systems or data, with 1 month to 1 year where the target is a public body or a public or financial service provider. Article 6 replaces Art. 155 on publication of private correspondence, with fines and an exemption for acts protecting a public interest. Articles 7 and 8 cover officials revealing secrets and offences involving personal data banks. Article 9 adds computer fraud by manipulation of information systems to Art. 173. Article 10 adds damage to data, programs or systems and distribution of damaging programs to Art. 183. Article 11 aggravates damage (Art. 184) where computer systems of public data or of health, communications, energy or transport services are targeted. Article 12 covers interference with communications and Article 13 covers tampering with evidence. Article 14 repeals Arts. 78 bis and 117 bis(1). The text states no separate entry-into-force date.},

title: Ley 27.506 - Régimen de Promoción de la Economía del Conocimiento
summary_short: Argentine statute, in force until 31 December 2029, creating a national promotion regime for knowledge-economy firms, including software, cloud services and Industry 4.0 automation using technologies such as AI. Registered firms meeting export, training, R&D or quality tests receive tax-credit bonuses on employer contributions, income-tax reductions and VAT withholding exemptions.
summary_long: Law 27.506 (2019) creates the Régimen de Promoción de la Economía del Conocimiento for the whole national territory. Article 2 lists promoted activities: software and digital services (including cloud computing and software embedded in processors), audiovisual production, biotechnology, aerospace, nanotechnology, nuclear engineering, selected export professional services, and Industry 4.0 automation solutions using technologies such as artificial intelligence, robotics and the industrial internet. Legal persons register in a national registry (Arts. 3–4) if at least 70% of last-year billing comes from promoted activities, or if they show intensive development of such activities, and if they meet at least two of three requirements: quality improvement, training or R&D investment as a share of payroll or billing, or exports. Registration is revalidated every two years; micro firms have simplified access (Art. 6). Benefits include a tax-credit bond for up to 70% of employer social-security contributions, raised to 80% for certain new hires (Arts. 8–9), income-tax reductions of 60%, 40% or 20% by firm size (Art. 10), and no VAT withholding on exports (Art. 11). Sanctions include suspension, revocation, payment of unpaid taxes and fines up to 100% of the benefit (Art. 15). A trust fund (FONPEC) finances promoted activities (Art. 18). Provinces and municipalities are invited to adopt analogous rules (Art. 22).

title: Ley 27.699 - Protección de las personas con respecto al tratamiento automatizado de datos de carácter personal. Protocolo modificatorio (Convenio 108+)
summary_short: Argentine statute approving the protocol amending Council of Europe Convention 108 (ETS 108+), signed in Strasbourg on 10 October 2018. The protocol sets data-protection principles, data-subject rights, transfer limits and supervisory-authority duties for Parties; its entry into force is governed by Art. 37 of the protocol.
summary_long: Law 27699 approves the Protocol amending Convention 108 (ETS 108+), signed in Strasbourg on 10 October 2018 (Art. 1). The amended Convention protects every person, whatever nationality or residence, in processing of personal data under a Party's jurisdiction, excluding purely personal or domestic activities. Processing must be lawful, proportionate and limited by purpose, minimisation, accuracy and storage principles. Sensitive data, including genetic, criminal and uniquely identifying biometric data, may be processed only with appropriate legal safeguards. Controllers must inform data subjects, secure data and notify serious breaches without delay. Data subjects may not be subject to significant decisions based solely on automated processing, may obtain the reasoning behind results, and may object and seek rectification. Controllers must demonstrate compliance, assess probable impact before processing, and minimise risk by design. Transfers to recipients under non-Party jurisdiction require an appropriate level of protection. Parties must establish supervisory authorities with investigation and sanction powers, and a Convention Committee is created. Entry into force follows Art. 37 of the Protocol, which repeals Additional Protocol ETS 181 on entry into force.

title: Ley 27.736 - Ley Olimpia (modificación de la Ley 26.485 de protección integral a las mujeres)
summary_short: Amends Ley 26.485 to define digital and telematic violence against women, add digital rights and digital literacy duties, and let courts order alleged aggressors to avoid digital contact and platforms to remove content and preserve data for 90 days. Entry-into-force date not stated.
summary_long: Amends Ley 26.485 on protection of women from violence. Adds digital rights to its objectives and dignity principle, and extends the definition of violence against women to acts committed or aggravated with information and communication technologies, in analog or digital space. Digital violence covers non-consensual distribution of real or edited intimate material, misogynist hate speech, harassment, threats, extortion, espionage and unauthorized access to accounts. It requires a free multi-channel reporting service, digital literacy in education, free judicial proceedings with digital forensic evidence, and protective orders: the alleged aggressor may be ordered to cease digital intimidation and to avoid contact through any technology. Courts may order platforms, social networks or websites, by reasoned order specifying the URL, to remove content and preserve traffic, subscriber and content data for 90 days, renewable once, with disclosure of subscriber data on request. The text states no penalties and no entry-into-force date; its dateline shows a publication notice dated 23/10/2023.

title: Ley 27.742 - Ley de Bases y Puntos de Partida para la Libertad de los Argentinos, Título VII: Régimen de Incentivo para Grandes Inversiones (RIGI)
summary_short: Ley 27.742 declares a one-year public emergency in administrative, economic, financial and energy matters and delegates listed powers to the executive. Title VII creates the RIGI investment incentive regime for large projects in listed sectors, open for two years from entry into force.
summary_long: Ley 27.742 declares a one-year public emergency in administrative, economic, financial and energy matters and delegates listed powers to the executive. It reorganises state bodies and companies, privatises named state firms, amends administrative procedure (Law 19.549), public and private employment rules, concession rules, and hydrocarbon, gas and electricity regimes, including export authorisations, royalties and a unified energy regulator. Title VII creates the RIGI investment incentive regime for single-project vehicles in listed sectors: minimum computable investment of USD 200 million (sector amounts up to USD 900 million), a 40% investment condition for the first two years, local supplier commitments, and approval by the enforcement authority within 45 days. Approved projects receive 30-year stability guarantees; adhesion is open for two years from entry into force, extendable once by one year. Only part 1 of 2 was supplied (through Art. 179); this annotation covers that portion.

title: Resolución 264/2026 - Secretaría de Energía (Ministerio de Economía) - Demandas Extratendenciales (XDEM) en el Mercado Eléctrico Mayorista
summary_short: Sets rules for new or expanded wholesale-market demands of at least 0.5% of average MEM demand (XDEM), with data-processing and production subcategories: registration, prior enablement, a supply plan, 80% contracted new energy, 100% or 115% new firm capacity, surcharges and technical specifications. In force 25 September 2026.
summary_long: Res. SE 264/2026 replaces Article 13 of Resolución SE 400/2025 and approves an annex, inserted as Appendix C of Annex 17 of 'Los Procedimientos', on Extratrend Demands (XDEM): new or expanded demand joining the wholesale electricity market (MEM) equal to or above 0.5% of average reference MEM demand. Demand of one project or linked group may not be split to avoid the threshold. XDEM are a subcategory of Large Major Users (GUMA): XDEM-DATOS (data centres, AI training or inference) and XDEM-PRODUCCIÓN (industry, mining, LNG, hydrogen). An XDEM registers with the Energy Secretariat, files a sworn five-year Special Supply Plan, is evaluated by the dispatch body (CAMMESA) and needs the Secretariat's prior enablement. It must contract each month at least 80% of its energy, and firm capacity of 100% (115% for XDEM-DATOS) of maximum demand, from new eligible supply. Uncovered energy pays the period energy value plus 100% (DATOS) or 50% (PRODUCCIÓN); uncovered capacity pays the large-user capacity charge plus 400% or 200%. Capacity awaiting transmission expansions costs USD 2,500/MW per quarter, partly refundable. A sub-annex sets connection studies and performance requirements. The regime applies for 15 years from commercial enablement; pending applications must adapt within 60 days.
text_version: original as published (BORA 2026-09-25); the text mentions no later amendments

title: Proyecto de ley: Régimen de Incentivo para Grandes Inversiones en Nuevas Industrias ("Súper RIGI") (Expte. 5-PE-2026; CD-6/26)
summary_short: Bill creating the Súper RIGI investment-incentive regime for approved projects of at least US$1,000 million in new industries. Approved project vehicles get reduced income tax, customs, VAT, FX and social-security benefits, with 30-year stability. Applies nationally; provincial benefits require adhesion. Enters into force the day after publication.
summary_long: Bill (Expte. 5-P.E.-2026, Orden del Día 149, majority committee report of 17 June 2026) creating the Régimen de Incentivo para Grandes Inversiones en Nuevas Industrias (Súper RIGI). Projects dedicated exclusively to new economic activities may join through Vehículos de Proyecto Único (VPU) if they commit at least US$1,000 million in qualifying assets, with 20% within the first two years (Arts. 4, 6, 12). The Autoridad de Aplicación approves or rejects applications within 90 business days (Art. 18). Approved VPU receive a 15% income tax rate, accelerated depreciation, customs and export-duty exemptions, VAT settlement through tax credit certificates, a 10% employer contribution rate for new employment relations, and FX-market relief. Dividends paid to individuals are taxed at 7%, falling to 3.5% after four years (Arts. 34–71). Tax, customs, social-security and FX rules are stabilised for 30 years (Arts. 75–84). Provinces and municipalities may not impose new local taxes, and gross-income tax is capped at 0.5%, conditional on their adhesion (Arts. 2, 113). Sanctions include warnings, fines and cessation of benefits (Arts. 92–100). Disputes may go to international arbitration (Arts. 109–111). Two minority reports recommend rejection.

title: Bundesgesetz zum Schutz natuerlicher Personen bei der Verarbeitung personenbezogener Daten (Datenschutzgesetz - DSG)
summary_short: Austrian Data Protection Act (DSG) that supplements and implements the GDPR for controllers and processors, and implements Directive (EU) 2016/680 for competent authorities (Part 3). It sets a fundamental right to data protection, data subject rights, controller duties and image-recording rules, and creates the Data Protection Authority. Original provisions in force from 1 January 2000 (§ 70(1)).
summary_long: The Datenschutzgesetz regulates processing of personal data in Austria alongside Regulation (EU) 2016/679 (Part 1, Art. 2) and, in Part 3, processing by competent authorities for criminal-law, security and intelligence purposes under Directive (EU) 2016/680. It sets out the constitutional right to data protection (§ 1), a minimum age of 14 for a child's consent to information-society services (§ 4(4)), and specific rules for processing for archiving, research and statistics (§ 7), address transfers (§ 8), journalistic and expressive purposes (§ 9, with exemptions from several GDPR articles), and disasters (§ 10). Part 1 also restricts image recording by private controllers, including a prohibition on recording for employee monitoring (§ 12(4)) and labelling duties (§ 13(5)). It creates the Data Protection Authority (§§ 18-35) and the Parliamentary Data Protection Committee (§§ 35a-35j). Controllers and processors bear duties on records, security, breach notification and data protection impact assessments (§§ 46-57 for Part 3). Part 3 prohibits decisions based solely on automated processing unless provided by law, and prohibits discrimination based on protected categories (§ 41). Sanctions include administrative fines by the authority (§§ 22(5), 30), administrative offences of up to 50,000 euro (§ 62), a court penalty of up to one year's imprisonment or fines (§ 63), and civil damages (§ 29). Some provisions are constitutional, and the text notes exemptions and limits for particular authorities and cases.]} ,

title: Bundesgesetz ueber Massnahmen zum Schutz der Nutzer auf Kommunikationsplattformen (Kommunikationsplattformen-Gesetz - KoPl-G), BGBl. I Nr. 151/2020
summary_short: Austrian statute requiring profit-oriented providers of large communication platforms to run notice-and-takedown and review procedures for unlawful content, publish reports, appoint a responsible officer, and face KommAustria supervision and fines, from 1 January 2021.
summary_long: The Kommunikationsplattformen-Gesetz (KoPl-G) applies to domestic and foreign profit-oriented providers of communication platforms, except where both user numbers are under 100,000 and Austrian turnover is under EUR 500,000. It also excludes marketplaces, non-profit encyclopedias, educational platforms and media outlets, and video-sharing platforms for their broadcasts and user videos. Providers must run an effective, transparent notice procedure: remove or block manifestly unlawful content within 24 hours and other unlawful content within seven days, preserve removed content and identifying data for up to ten weeks, and offer a review procedure with a two-week application period. They must publish reports, half-yearly above one million registered users, and appoint a responsible officer and a service agent. Users may complain to a complaints body (Beschwerdestelle) supported by RTR-GmbH. KommAustria supervises compliance, may order providers by decision to restore lawful conditions, and may impose fines of up to EUR 10 million for listed breaches, up to EUR 1 million for failing to appoint a responsible officer after a request, and up to EUR 58,000 for refusing information. Measures may not amount to general ex-ante content control. The Act entered into force on 1 January 2021, and existing providers had until 31 March 2021 to comply.

title: Privacy and Other Legislation Amendment Act 2024 (No. 128, 2024)
summary_short: Commonwealth Act amending the Privacy Act 1988 and other federal laws. Schedule 1 reforms cover APP codes, children's privacy, security, overseas data flows, eligible data breaches, penalties, and automated decisions. Schedule 2 adds serious invasions of privacy; Schedule 3 adds doxxing offences to the Criminal Code Act 1995.
summary_long: The Privacy and Other Legislation Amendment Act 2024 (No. 128, 2024) is a Commonwealth Act. The supplied document is the Federal Register page showing only the table of contents, not the operative text, so this annotation rests on the provision headings. Schedule 1 (Privacy reforms) has fifteen Parts that amend the Privacy Act 1988 on: objects; APP codes; emergency declarations; children's privacy; security, retention and destruction; overseas data flows; eligible data breaches; penalties for interference with privacy; Federal Court orders; public inquiries by the Commissioner; determinations; annual reports; external dispute resolution; monitoring and investigation; and automated decisions and privacy policies. Several Parts also list amendments to other Commonwealth Acts, including the Data Availability and Transparency Act 2022, Digital ID Act 2024, Identity Verification Services Act 2023, Competition and Consumer Act 2010, Crimes Act 1914, Data matching Program (Assistance and Tax) Act 1990 and National Health Act 1953. Schedule 2 concerns serious invasions of privacy, and Schedule 3 creates doxxing offences in the Criminal Code Act 1995. Section 4 provides for a review of the operation of the Schedule 3 amendments. Commencement dates are set out in section 2, which is not included in the supplied text.

title: Online Safety Amendment (Social Media Minimum Age) Act 2024 (No. 127, 2024)
summary_short: Amends the Online Safety Act 2021 to require providers of age-restricted social media platforms to take reasonable steps to prevent Australian children under 16 from having accounts. Civil penalties and privacy limits apply; the duty starts on a day set by the Minister.
summary_long: The Act adds Part 4A on social media minimum age to the Online Safety Act 2021. An age-restricted social media platform is an electronic service whose sole or significant purpose is online social interaction between end-users, with exclusions and additions by legislative rules (s 63C). Providers must take reasonable steps to prevent Australian children under 16 from having accounts (s 63D; 30,000 penalty units). The duty starts on a day set by the Minister, no later than 12 months after commencement (s 63E). Providers may not collect specified information or government identification or accredited Digital ID services for compliance (ss 63DA, 63DB; 30,000 penalty units each). Compliance information is restricted to age determination, specified exceptions and consent, and must be destroyed after use; breaches are treated as privacy interferences (s 63F). The eSafety Commissioner may require information (non-compliance: 500 penalty units), publish contravention statements and formulate non-legislative guidelines. Schedule 1 also raises penalties in ss 143(2) and 146 of the Online Safety Act, and the Minister must commission an independent review within two years after s 63D takes effect. Commenced 11 December 2024.
text_version: Act as made (No. 127, 2024), authorised version C2024A00127 registered 12/12/2024

title: Resolução Anatel nº 740, de 21 de dezembro de 2020 - Aprova o Regulamento de Segurança Cibernética Aplicada ao Setor de Telecomunicações (R-Ciber)
summary_short: Approves Anatel's R-Ciber regulation on cybersecurity for telecommunications service providers of collective interest, excluding small-size providers, requiring a cybersecurity policy, incident notification and vulnerability assessments; effective 4 January 2021.
summary_long: Approves the Regulamento de Segurança Cibernética Aplicada ao Setor de Telecomunicações (R-Ciber), adopted by Anatel's Conselho Diretor and in force from 4 January 2021. It applies to telecommunications service providers of collective interest other than small-size providers (Art. 2). Providers must maintain a cybersecurity policy approved by their board, with a non-sensitive extract published online (Arts. 6, 13-15), use suppliers with compatible policies and periodic independent audits (Art. 7), change default authentication on equipment lent to users (Art. 8), notify Anatel of relevant incidents and communicate them to other providers and users (Arts. 9, 17), commission independent vulnerability assessments (Arts. 10, 19), send data on critical telecommunications infrastructure (Arts. 11, 20), and file an annual report (Art. 16). Resolution 767/2024 extended Art. 8 to small providers (Art. 2-A) and applied some duties to operators identified in a Superintendency ordinance (Art. 2-B). The regulation creates the GT-Ciber working group (Art. 24) and lets Anatel impose specific technical requirements (Art. 23). Infringements are subject to sanctions under Lei 9.472/1997 and Anatel's sanctions regulation (Art. 25). Providers have 180 days from entry into force to comply (Art. 27).

title: Resolução Anatel nº 777, de 28 de abril de 2025 - Revoga e altera Resoluções e aprova o Regulamento Geral dos Serviços de Telecomunicações (RGST)
summary_short: Anatel Resolution 777/2025 approves the General Telecommunications Services Regulation (RGST), revoking or replacing numerous earlier Anatel rules. Binding on telecom service providers: licensing, interconnection, number portability, emergency services, fraud prevention, subscriber data and consumer duties. Article 40 sets principles for providers' AI-based solutions. Generally in force 180 days after publication.
summary_long: Anatel Resolution 777/2025 approves the General Telecommunications Services Regulation (RGST), annexed to it, and revokes, replaces or amends numerous earlier Anatel regulations (Arts. 1-26). The Annex sets rules for public and private telecom services, authorization and licensing, equipment certification and networks. Article 40 requires providers using AI-based solutions to observe listed principles, including reliability, non-discrimination, privacy and transparency and explainability. Other provisions cover interconnection, number portability through a central database and an administering entity, provider and user duties, record retention for set periods, free access to emergency services, secrecy and data retention limits, fraud prevention, maximum charges for certain shared-rate calls, and mandatory distribution of certain TV channels. Sanctions are referred to other regulation (Art. 40 sole paragraph; Art. 43 §6); no penalty amounts appear in this text. Most provisions apply from 180 days after publication (Art. 28), and the header notes that some deadlines were postponed by Anatel orders. The document provided covers the instrument through Title V, Chapter II of the Annex.

title: Resolução Anatel nº 780, de 1º de agosto de 2025 - Altera o Regulamento de Avaliação da Conformidade e de Homologação de Produtos para Telecomunicações (Título VI-A: data centers que integram as redes de telecomunicações)
summary_short: Amends Anatel's telecom product conformity and homologation rules: makes online marketplaces jointly liable with sellers for non-homologated products, widens sanctionable conduct, and adds a Title VI-A requiring conformity assessment of telecom-network data centers before operation (its enforceability is suspended per the document).
summary_long: Amends Anatel's telecom product conformity and homologation regulation (Resolução 715/2019). Art. 1 revokes two provisions. Art. 2 makes marketplaces and other digital platforms involved in selling a product jointly liable with the seller, including for disclosing and checking its homologation code. Art. 3 revises arts. 83-85 to list sanctionable conduct, extends responsibility to platforms for irregular online offers, and allows removal of designated bodies after due process. Art. 4 limits certification of reconditioned products to public-policy purposes; Art. 5 applies the Consumer Protection Code subsidiarily. Art. 6 adds Title VI-A: data centers integrated into telecom networks need conformity assessment before operation, under a procedure due within 240 days; providers may then install or contract only certified new centers, and existing ones have three years to comply. Requirements cover continuous operation, physical and cyber security, energy efficiency and environmental practices. As the document notes, Acórdão nº 58 of 3 March 2026 suspended Art. 6's enforceability pending reassessment. Art. 7: in force on publication, except Arts. 2 and 3, which take effect four months later.

title: Resolução CD/ANPD nº 15, de 24 de abril de 2024 - Regulamento de Comunicação de Incidente de Segurança
summary_short: Sets procedures for controllers to report security incidents posing relevant risk or harm to data subjects to the ANPD and to data subjects within three business days of knowledge, and to keep incident records for at least five years. Takes effect on publication (April 2024).
summary_long: Approves the Regulamento de Comunicação de Incidente de Segurança under LGPD art. 48. It requires controllers to communicate to the ANPD and to affected data subjects any security incident that may cause relevant risk or damage to data subjects, where the incident can significantly affect fundamental interests and rights and involves at least one listed criterion (sensitive data, data of children, adolescents or elderly, financial data, system authentication data, secret-protected data, or large-scale data). The ANPD communication is due within three business days of knowledge, with a prescribed set of contents, supplementable within twenty business days, submitted through an ANPD electronic form. The data-subject communication is due within the same period, in plain language and directly, or through public disclosure kept visible for at least three months where direct contact is unfeasible. Controllers must keep incident records for at least five years. The ANPD may request information and audits, order preventive measures with daily fines, open proceedings against unreported incidents, and order broad media disclosure at the controller's expense. Small-size processing agents have doubled deadlines. The regulation applies to ongoing processes on entry into force.

title: Resolução CD/ANPD nº 19, de 23 de agosto de 2024 - Regulamento de Transferência Internacional de Dados e conteúdo das cláusulas-padrão contratuais
summary_short: Brazil's ANPD regulation (Resolução CD/ANPD 19/2024) governs international transfers of personal data: adequacy decisions, ANPD-approved standard and specific clauses, and global corporate rules. It binds controllers and processors transferring data abroad, effective on publication, with a 12-month deadline to incorporate the standard clauses.
summary_long: Annex I (Regulamento de Transferência Internacional de Dados) is based on Articles 33 to 36 of the Brazilian General Data Protection Law (LGPD, Law 13.709/2018). It defines international data transfers (Arts. 3 to 6), extends national law to processing in Brazil, to offers of goods or services to individuals in Brazil, and to data collected in Brazil regardless of where the agents are based (Art. 7), and sets the legal bases and transfer mechanisms (Art. 9). It covers ANPD adequacy decisions for foreign countries and international organisations (Arts. 10 to 14), standard contractual clauses that ANPD approves and that must be adopted without alteration (Arts. 15 to 20), and specific contractual clauses and global corporate rules that require prior ANPD approval (Arts. 21 to 33). Annex II sets out the standard clauses: transparency publication, data subject rights, security measures, incident notification within 3 business days, liability, and additional safeguards for sensitive data and children's data. Under the resolution's operative article, controllers using contractual clauses must incorporate the approved standard clauses into their contracts within 12 months of publication. The instrument takes effect on publication. ANPD may limit, suspend or prohibit transfers and apply administrative sanctions (Annex II, Clause 7).

title: Resolução CD/ANPD nº 2, de 27 de janeiro de 2022 - Regulamento de aplicação da LGPD para agentes de tratamento de pequeno porte
summary_short: ANPD resolution approving a regulation applying Brazil's LGPD to small personal-data processing agents (microempresas, small businesses, startups, and similar entities). Allows simplified compliance on records, DPO, security policy and response deadlines, excluding high-risk processing and agents above revenue limits. In force on publication.
summary_long: The resolution approves the regulation applying the LGPD to small processing agents. Its scope covers microempresas, empresas de pequeno porte, startups and similar entities, including individuals and unincorporated entities that act as controllers or operators (Art. 2). Agents are excluded if they carry out high-risk processing or exceed the gross revenue limits of the small-business or startup laws, alone or through an economic group (Art. 3). High-risk processing requires at least one general criterion (large-scale processing or significant effect on rights) and one specific criterion (emerging technologies, surveillance of public areas, solely automated decisions, or sensitive, children's, adolescents' or elderly persons' data) (Art. 4). Eligible agents may keep simplified records (Art. 9), need not appoint a DPO if they provide a contact channel (Art. 11), adopt essential security measures and may adopt a simplified security policy (Arts. 12-13), and receive doubled deadlines for responding to data-subject requests and reporting incidents (Art. 14). Art. 6 states that the relief does not exempt agents from other LGPD provisions. The ANPD may require compliance with waived obligations (Art. 16). The text sets no penalties of its own. It takes effect on publication (Art. 2), and its Art. 14 II was amended by Resolução CD/ANPD nº 15/2024.

title: Resolução CD/ANPD nº 32, de 26 de janeiro de 2026 - Reconhecimento da União Europeia como organismo internacional com grau de proteção de dados pessoais adequado (transferência internacional)
summary_short: Recognises the European Union, its member states, the EEA states Iceland, Liechtenstein and Norway, and EU institutions as providing an adequate level of personal data protection, so that international transfers may rely on LGPD Art. 33 I. Excludes transfers for public security, defence, state security and criminal investigation. Enters into force on publication.
summary_long: ANPD Resolução CD/ANPD nº 32 of 26 January 2026, published in the Diário Oficial da União on 27 January 2026, recognises the European Union as an international organisation providing an adequate level of personal data protection under the Lei nº 13.709/2018 (LGPD). Art. 1 paragraph single authorises international data transfers under LGPD Art. 33 I to all EU member states, the EEA states Iceland, Liechtenstein and Norway, and EU institutions, bodies and agencies, referring to Regulation (EU) 2016/679, EEA Joint Committee Decision 154/2018 and Regulation (EU) 2018/1725. Art. 2 excludes transfers made exclusively for public security, national defence, State security or criminal investigation and prosecution. Art. 3 allows the ANPD to set up cooperation mechanisms with the European Commission and European data protection authorities. Art. 4 requires the ANPD to monitor the EU level of protection on a continuing basis, may request information and carry out periodic assessments, and provides for reassessment within four years of entry into force, taking into account later changes to EU data protection law. Art. 5 states that the decision does not prevent transfers to those countries under the other transfer mechanisms of LGPD Art. 33. Art. 6 sets entry into force on the date of publication. The resolution was adopted by the ANPD Conselho Diretor under LGPD Art. 34 and internal regulations, citing Resolução CD/ANPD nº 19/2024.

title: Resolução CD/ANPD nº 4, de 24 de fevereiro de 2023 - Regulamento de Dosimetria e Aplicação de Sanções Administrativas
summary_short: Brazil's data protection authority (ANPD) approves a regulation setting the methodology for calculating administrative sanctions under the LGPD, including infraction classes, aggravating and mitigating factors, and fine caps. It also amends the ANPD's sanctioning procedure rules and takes effect on publication.
summary_long: Resolution CD/ANPD No. 4 of 24 February 2023 approves the Regulation on Dosimetry and Application of Administrative Sanctions of Brazil's National Data Protection Authority (ANPD), which applies to infractions of the LGPD and ANPD regulations. Infractions are classified as light, medium or serious (Art. 8). Sanctions include warning, simple fine, daily fine, publicization, blocking, deletion, suspension of a database or processing activity, and prohibition of data-processing activities (Art. 3). The base value of a simple fine follows a methodology in Appendix I using the infringer's revenue, the infraction class and the degree of damage (Art. 11). Aggravating circumstances add up to 40%, 20%, 80% and 90%, and mitigating circumstances reduce the amount (Arts. 12-14). The result is subject to minimum values in Appendix II and capped at 2% of Brazilian revenue or R$ 50,000,000 (Art. 15). Daily fines accrue up to R$ 50,000,000 per infraction (Art. 16). Database or processing suspensions last at most six months, extendable once (Arts. 24-25). Payment is due within 20 business days, with a 25% reduction for waiving appeal (Arts. 17-18). The resolution also amends the ANPD's enforcement procedure rules (Art. 2), applies to ongoing proceedings (Art. 28) and takes effect on publication (Art. 4 of the resolution). The appendices are referenced but not reproduced in the fetched text.

title: Resolução Conjunta nº 1, de 4 de maio de 2020 - Dispõe sobre a implementação do Open Finance
summary_short: Joint resolution of the Banco Central do Brasil and the National Monetary Council implementing Open Banking in Brazil. It sets rules for sharing customer data and services, consent, authentication and interfaces for institutions authorized by the Central Bank, phased in from 1 June 2020 to 25 October 2021.
summary_long: Joint resolution of the Banco Central do Brasil and the National Monetary Council implementing Open Banking (Sistema Financeiro Aberto). It applies to financial institutions, payment institutions and other institutions authorized by the Central Bank (Art. 1). Participation is mandatory for S1 and S2 institutions for certain data and services, and voluntary for others (Art. 6). Customer consent must be specific, valid for up to twelve months unless the customer sets a longer period for successive payments, and cannot be given through adhesion contracts, pre-filled forms or presumed consent (Art. 10). Consent, authentication, confirmation and revocation steps apply (Arts. 8, 15-20). Institutions must offer standardized dedicated interfaces and must not create obstacles to sharing (Arts. 23, 28). Partnerships with non-authorized entities require prior due diligence and contract terms, including Central Bank access (Arts. 36-38). Each institution designates a responsible director, files semi-annual reports and keeps records for five years (Arts. 32-33, 49). Technical standards are set by a participants' convention subject to Central Bank approval (Arts. 44, 47). Phased deadlines run from 1 June 2020 to 25 October 2021 (Art. 55). The text sets no fine amounts; the Central Bank may veto or restrict partnerships (Art. 52).

title: Resolução BCB nº 85, de 8 de abril de 2021 - Dispõe sobre a política de segurança cibernética e os requisitos para contratação de serviços de processamento e armazenamento de dados e de computação em nuvem por instituições de pagamento e outras
summary_short: Requires Central Bank-authorised payment institutions (and, as amended, certain brokers and virtual asset providers) to adopt a cybersecurity policy and incident plan and follow rules for contracting cloud and data-processing services, including notification and conditions for services abroad. Applies from 1 August 2021.
summary_long: Sets cybersecurity policy and cloud-contracting rules for payment institutions and, under later amendments, certain securities brokers and distributors, foreign-exchange brokers and virtual asset service providers authorised by the Central Bank of Brazil. Each institution must adopt a cybersecurity policy with minimum contents, approved by its board and reviewed annually, plus an incident response plan; it must publish a policy summary, designate a responsible director and report annually on the plan. Before contracting relevant cloud or data-processing services, it must follow verification procedures, include specified contract clauses, and notify the Central Bank within ten days. Services provided abroad require a Central Bank information-sharing agreement with the foreign supervisor or prior Central Bank authorisation requested sixty days in advance. The Central Bank may veto or restrict contracting for non-compliance. Records must be kept for five years. The Resolution took effect on 1 August 2021; the text reflects amendments by Resolutions 368/2024, 538/2025 and 552/2026.

title: Lei nº 14.968, de 11 de setembro de 2024 - cria o Programa Brasil Semicondutores (Brasil Semicon) e aperfeiçoa a política industrial para TIC e semicondutores
summary_short: Law 14.968/2024 creates the Brasil Semicon program and amends tax, R&D credit and Padis rules for semiconductor, display, solar-panel and ICT manufacturers in Brazil. It takes effect 1 January 2025, and its incentives run until 31 December 2029.
summary_long: Law 14.968/2024 creates the Programa Brasil Semicondutores (Brasil Semicon) to support research, design, production and application of semiconductor components, displays and solar panels in Brazil (Art. 3). It authorizes a management council (Art. 4) and BNDES and Finep to structure financing and minority equity support for firms enrolled in Padis (Art. 5). It amends Decree-Law 288/1967 (10-percentage-point increase for nationally developed ICT products, Art. 6), Law 8.248/1991 (R&D financial credit and reporting duties, Art. 7), Law 13.969/2019 (credit multipliers and caps, Art. 8) and Law 11.484/2007 (Art. 9). Under Law 11.484, Padis enrolment requires a specific act conditioned on tax compliance; enrolled firms get reduced rates on PIS/Cofins, IPI and import duty, a 100% income-tax reduction on device sales, and must invest at least 5% of incentivised gross revenue in R&D yearly. Non-compliance causes loss of the reduction and payment of the tax with interest and late-payment fine. The Ministry of Science, Technology and Innovation defines rules on nationally developed technology (Art. 10). Incentives run until 31 December 2029 (Art. 11); the law takes effect 1 January 2025 (Art. 13).

title: Federal Senate Bill of Law No. 2338, of 2023
summary_short: Senate bill setting national rules for AI systems in Brazil. Grants affected persons rights to information, explanation and contestation; prohibits excessive-risk systems; imposes duties on high-risk systems, including impact assessments; sets civil liability and administrative sanctions; enters into force one year after publication.
summary_long: Federal Senate Bill No. 2338/2023 would set general national rules for the development, implementation and use of AI systems in Brazil, based on listed principles. It grants persons affected by AI systems rights to prior information, explanation of decisions, contestation and human review, and non-discrimination. Article 14 prohibits systems that use subliminal techniques, exploit vulnerabilities of specific groups, or are used by the public power for universal scoring. Article 15 restricts remote biometric identification in public spaces. Article 13 requires a preliminary risk assessment by the provider, and the competent authority updates the list of excessive and high-risk systems (Arts. 17-18). Providers and operators of high-risk systems must adopt governance measures, documentation, testing and algorithmic impact assessments (Arts. 20-26). Civil liability is objective for high- and excessive-risk systems and presumed-fault otherwise (Art. 27). The Executive designates a competent authority (Art. 32). Administrative sanctions include a fine limited to R$ 50,000,000.00 per infraction or 2% of revenue (Art. 36). Article 42 sets a text and data mining exception for listed bodies. The law would enter into force one year after publication (Art. 45).](Filler)

title: Lei nº 19.849, de 16 de julho de 2026 - Institui a Política Estadual de Incentivo à Implantação de Sistemas de Armazenamento de Energia em Baterias (SAEB) e de data centers e centros de processamento de dados no Ceará
summary_short: Ceará state statute (Lei 19.849/2026) creating an incentive policy for battery energy storage systems (SAEB) and data centers. It sets size-based environmental licensing stages and study requirements, allows public land allocation and ICMS tax relief subject to Confaz agreement, and imposes fire-safety and monitoring duties. Effective on publication, 16 July 2026.
summary_long: Lei 19.849 of 16 July 2026 establishes a state incentive policy for battery energy storage systems (SAEB) and data centers in Ceará. Articles 2 and 3 set environmental licensing stages by size and environmental potential: SAEB of small size use a single licence (LAU), medium and large SAEB use two stages (LP and LIO), and exceptional SAEB use three stages (LP, LI and LO); data centers of small and medium size use two stages and large and exceptional data centers use three. Article 4 and the Annex classify projects into micro, small, medium, large and exceptional bands by capacity (MWh for SAEB, MW for data centers). Article 5 assigns micro projects to municipal environmental bodies, or to Semace where none is qualified. Article 6 links the required environmental study to size. Article 7 directs Semace to issue a normative instruction, and Article 7-A requires medium-and-larger data centers to keep continuous environmental monitoring. Article 8 requires the state Fire Department to issue fire-safety technical standards. Article 9 allows state land near transmission substations to be allocated to SAEB projects through public selection. Article 10 allows ICMS deferral or exemption on equipment, conditional on Confaz agreement. Articles 11 and 12 assign coordination to the State Development Secretariat and authorise cooperation agreements with federal bodies and grid entities. Entry into force on publication.

title: Resolução CFM nº 2.454, de 11 de fevereiro de 2026 - Normatiza o uso da inteligência artificial na medicina
summary_short: CFM Resolution 2,454/2026 sets rules for research, development, governance, audit, monitoring and responsible use of AI in medicine. It applies to physicians and medical institutions, requires physician oversight, patient information, risk categorisation (low, medium, high) and governance measures, and takes effect 180 days after publication.
summary_long: Resolution CFM No. 2,454 of 11 February 2026 sets norms for research, development, governance, auditing, monitoring, training and responsible use of AI systems and models in medicine. Its addressees are physicians and medical institutions. They must keep final clinical authority with the physician (Arts. 4, 7, 18-19), inform patients when AI is used as relevant support (Art. 5 §1; Art. 11), protect health data and avoid AI tools without adequate information security (Art. 6), and respect fundamental rights and bioethics across the AI lifecycle (Art. 9). Institutions must perform a preliminary risk assessment (Art. 12) and classify AI solutions as low, medium, high or unacceptable risk under Annex II, informing users of the classification (Art. 13). Annex III lists governance measures, including bias monitoring and mitigation, an algorithmic impact assessment and a Technical Director responsible for oversight. Institutions with in-house systems must create an AI and Telemedicine Committee (Art. 14). Supervision is by the regional medical councils (Art. 15). Violations lead to ethical sanctions, without prejudice to civil and criminal liability (Art. 8). The rules also cover systems in use at entry into force (Art. 21) and the resolution takes effect 180 days after publication (Art. 23).

title: Resolução CMN nº 4.893, de 26 de fevereiro de 2021 - Dispõe sobre a política de segurança cibernética e os requisitos para contratação de serviços de processamento e armazenamento de dados e de computação em nuvem pelas instituições autorizadas pelo Banco Central
summary_short: Requires institutions authorized by the Central Bank of Brazil to adopt a cybersecurity policy and incident response plan, and to meet conditions for relevant cloud and data processing contracts, including notice to and authorization by the central bank for overseas services. Effective 1 July 2021.
summary_long: Requires institutions authorized by the Central Bank of Brazil (BCB) to adopt a board-approved cybersecurity policy with minimum controls (Arts. 2–3-A) and an incident response plan (Art. 6). Policies are disclosed to staff and third-party providers, and a summary to the public (Arts. 4–5). Institutions designate a responsible director, file an annual report and review policies yearly (Arts. 7–10). Contracting of relevant data processing, storage and cloud computing services requires prior governance and provider checks (Art. 12) and notice to the BCB within ten days (Art. 15). For overseas services, institutions need an information-exchange agreement with the relevant supervisors or, absent one, BCB authorization requested at least sixty days in advance (Art. 16). Contracts must include minimum clauses on data location, segregation, subcontracting notice and BCB access (Art. 17). Business continuity, monitoring, incident information sharing and annual intrusion tests by independent parties follow (Arts. 19–22-A). The BCB may set further requirements (Art. 24) and may veto or restrict non-compliant contracts (Art. 26). Pre-2018 contracts had to be adapted within a deadline not exceeding 31 December 2021 (Art. 25). The text sets no monetary penalties.

title: Decreto nº 12.772, de 5 de dezembro de 2025 - Institui a Política Nacional de Acesso ao Sistema de Transmissão (PNAST)
summary_short: Creates Brazil's National Transmission Access Policy (PNAST): from 8 December 2025, permanent access to the basic transmission grid and increases in contracted use go through periodic Access Seasons run by the ONS, with competitive processes where demand exceeds capacity. Sets transitional rules for pending requests; excludes distribution utilities.
summary_long: Decreto 12.772/2025 creates the PNAST for users seeking permanent access to the transmission system or more contracted transmission use; distribution concessionaires and permissionaires are excluded. Access to the basic grid and increases in contracted use occur through Access Seasons: periodic windows in which applicants register demand, analysed jointly by the national system operator (ONS). Where registered demand exceeds available capacity at a connection point, competitive processes are held; their revenues go to tariff moderation. Under ministry guidelines, these processes may cover future capacity, voluntary release of contracted amounts, capacity conditioned on investment, and margins for regional development. The first season must be held within ten months of publication and at least two a year from the following year, with schedules published 90 days ahead. Requests filed before publication receive access opinions within ten months, without priority for future margins or revalidation; interim requests need remaining capacity. Consumer requests pending at the ministry go to the ONS, subject to a 45-day financial guarantee, and the ministry plans grid expansions for them. EPE gains access to applicant data and runs an annual mapping call. Decreto 5.597/2005 is amended to cover multi-unit hubs or clusters at one connection point.

title: Decreto nº 12.880, de 18 de março de 2026 - Regulamenta a Lei nº 15.211/2025 (ECA Digital) e institui a Política Nacional de Promoção e Proteção dos Direitos da Criança e do Adolescente no Ambiente Digital
summary_short: Regulates Law 15.211/2025 (ECA Digital) on children's protection in digital environments: age assurance, prohibited-content access, advertising, reporting and transparency duties for information technology providers, app stores and operating systems; institutes a national children's digital policy. In force on publication, 18 March 2026.
summary_long: Implements Law 15.211/2025 (ECA Digital) and institutes a National Policy for Promotion and Protection of Children's and Adolescents' Rights in the Digital Environment, with an intersectoral committee and a Federal Police notification triage centre (Arts. 1-8). Providers of information technology products or services directed at or likely accessed by children must prevent excessive use and manipulative design (Arts. 9-10). Providers of generative and conversational AI services must disclose synthetic interaction, prevent behavioural manipulation, assess algorithmic risk and apply safeguards (Art. 11). Prohibited content (e.g., alcohol, tobacco, gambling, pornography, loot boxes) must be kept from children through age verification (Arts. 14-19). App stores and operating systems must supply age signals and seek parental authorisation for app downloads (Art. 25). Age-assurance methods must meet data-minimisation and privacy rules, with ANPD regulating and certifying them (Arts. 24-30). Child-directed advertising, profiling and monetised child content are restricted (Arts. 31-35). Providers must report serious child-abuse content to the triage centre, remove it, and offer notification mechanisms (Arts. 36-43); ANPD accredits child-rights NGOs (Art. 44). Larger providers report notification data (Art. 45) and conduct child-safety impact assessments (Art. 47). Until ANPD regulates, manufacturers and importers of devices marketed exclusively to children must add a parental-supervision warning on packaging (Art. 50).

title: Decreto nº 13.065, de 15 de julho de 2026 - Altera o Decreto nº 10.615/2021 (PADIS) e regulamenta o art. 3º da Lei nº 14.968/2024 (Programa Brasil Semicondutores)
summary_short: Decree 13.065/2026 amends Decree 10.615/2021 on the PADIS semiconductor programme and regulates Law 14.968/2024 by establishing the Brasil Semicon programme, a governing council, PADIS tax reductions, R&D investment duties, reporting and sanctions for habilitated firms. It concerns semiconductor industrial policy and contains no AI-specific provisions.
summary_long: Decree No. 13.065 of 15 July 2026 amends Decree No. 10.615/2021, which regulates the PADIS semiconductor industry development programme under Law 11.484/2007, and regulates Art. 3 of Law 14.968/2024 to set up the Brasil Semicon programme. It states the programme's objective (components, displays and solar panels), its axes and guidelines, and creates a Brasil Semicon Management Council chaired by the Ministry of Development, Industry, Trade and Services, with a monitoring and reporting cycle. Firms habilitated to PADIS, through acts of the Ministry of Science, Technology and Innovation, receive reductions to zero of federal taxes (PIS/Pasep, Cofins, IPI, import duty, AFRMM, IRPJ and CSLL) on listed equipment, software, inputs, technology payments and services, and a financial credit calculated on R&D spending (multiplier 2.62, capped at 13.10% of the investment base). Beneficiaries must invest at least 5% of gross revenue in R&D and file annual compliance statements and independently audited reports. Sanctions include suspension and cancellation of benefits, with an appeal to the ministry within thirty days. Some benefit provisions apply until 31 December 2029. The decree does not refer to artificial intelligence. It takes effect on the date of publication.

title: Lei nº 15.211, de 17 de setembro de 2025 - Estatuto Digital da Criança e do Adolescente
summary_short: Brazil's Digital Statute for Children and Adolescents (Lei 15.211/2025) requires providers of digital products or services directed at or likely accessed by minors to protect them through safety, age-assurance, parental supervision, content, advertising and reporting duties, enforced by an autonomous authority, effective 17 March 2026 per Art. 41-A.
summary_long: Lei nº 15.211/2025 (Estatuto Digital da Criança e do Adolescente) sets child-protection duties for information technology products and services directed to children and adolescents or likely to be accessed by them, wherever the provider is located (Art. 1). Chapters I and II set principles and general duties: priority protection and best interests (Art. 3), safety and privacy by design with protective default settings (Arts. 6-7), risk management and age-appropriate content (Art. 8). Chapters III and IV bar access to improper content and require age verification without self-declaration (Art. 9), with duties for app stores and operating systems to provide age signals and parental consent for app downloads (Art. 12). Chapters V to VII cover parental supervision tools and default settings (Arts. 16-18), child-monitoring products (Art. 19) and a ban on loot boxes in child-directed games (Art. 20). Chapters VIII and IX ban profiling-based advertising to children (Arts. 22, 26), require guardian-linked accounts for users up to 16 (Art. 24) and set social-network duties. Chapters X to XII cover removal and reporting of child-abuse content, notice-and-takedown and semi-annual transparency reports (Arts. 27-31). Chapter XIII addresses abusive use of reporting tools (Arts. 32-33). Chapter XIV assigns duties to an autonomous administrative authority (Art. 34). Chapter XV sets penalties: warning, per-user or turnover-based fines, suspension and prohibition, applied by the authority or the courts (Art. 35). Art. 39 modulates obligations by service features, reach and size. Art. 40 requires a legal representative in Brazil. Art. 41-A sets entry into force on 17 March 2026.

title: Lei nº 15.123, de 24 de abril de 2025 - altera o art. 147-B do Código Penal (violência psicológica contra a mulher com uso de inteligência artificial)
summary_short: Amends Article 147-B of the Brazilian Penal Code to add a paragraph under which the penalty for psychological violence against women is increased by half when committed using artificial intelligence or other technology that alters the victim's image or sound. Takes effect on publication.
summary_long: Law No. 15.123 of 24 April 2025 amends Article 147-B of the Brazilian Penal Code, which covers psychological violence against women, by adding a single paragraph. Under the new paragraph, the penalty is increased by half where the crime is committed using artificial intelligence or any other technological resource that alters the victim's image or sound. The law creates no new offence, authority, registration, labelling or platform duty, and it does not restate the base penalty or the Code's other sanctions. Article 3 provides that the law enters into force on the date of its publication. The text notes that it does not replace the version published in the official gazette (DOU) of 25 April 2025.

title: Lei nº 15.352, de 25 de fevereiro de 2026 - Conversão da MP nº 1.317/2025; altera a LGPD para dispor sobre a Agência Nacional de Proteção de Dados (ANPD) e a Lei nº 15.211/2025 (ECA Digital)
summary_short: Converts Provisional Measure 1.317/2025 and amends the LGPD to create the ANPD as a special-nature autarchy linked to the Ministry of Justice and Public Security. Creates a data protection regulation career and posts, and sets 17 March 2026 as the start of the ECA Digital. Takes effect on publication.
summary_long: Law 15.352/2026 converts Provisional Measure 1.317/2025 and amends the General Data Protection Law (LGPD, Law 13.709/2018). It adds definitions of 'encarregado' and 'autoridade nacional' and a new LGPD Chapter IX creating the ANPD as a special-nature autarchy linked to the Ministry of Justice and Public Security, with functional, technical, decision-making, administrative and financial autonomy. It creates a Data Protection Regulation and Inspection career in Law 10.871/2004 and transforms 797 vacant effective posts into 200 specialist posts and 18 commissioned or trust functions. Holders of the career posts are given prerogatives to order the interdiction of establishments and seize goods when exercising fiscal or police powers. The ANPD must publish a plan for adapting its regulation within 30 days of the publication of the act setting its new regimental structure. Law 15.211/2025 (ECA Digital) is amended so that it enters into force on 17 March 2026. Provisional Measure 1.319/2025 is revoked. The law takes effect on publication.

title: Lei nº 13.709, de 14 de agosto de 2018 - Lei Geral de Proteção de Dados Pessoais (LGPD)
summary_short: Brazil's general personal data protection law (LGPD) governs processing of personal data by public and private actors, where processing occurs in Brazil, targets people in Brazil, or data was collected there. It sets legal bases, data subject rights, controller and processor duties, international transfer rules, and ANPD sanctions.
summary_long: The LGPD (Law 13.709/2018) regulates processing of personal data, including in digital media, by natural and legal persons, public or private. Art. 3 covers processing carried out in Brazil, processing aimed at offering goods or services to people located in Brazil, and data collected there; Art. 4 excludes purely personal, journalistic, artistic, academic, public-security and defence uses. It sets legal bases (Art. 7), rules for sensitive, anonymised and children's data (Arts. 11–14), and data subject rights, including review of decisions made solely by automated processing (Arts. 18–22). Public bodies and international transfers are covered in Arts. 23–36. Controllers and operators face duties on records, impact reports, a data protection officer, liability, security and governance programmes (Arts. 37–51). Art. 52 provides administrative sanctions: warnings, fines of up to 2% of Brazilian revenue capped at R$50 million per infraction, publicising, blocking and deletion of data, and partial suspension or prohibition. Chapter IX creates the national authority (ANPD), later described as an agency, and a national council. Entry into force was phased under Art. 65.

title: Lei nº 12.965, de 23 de abril de 2014 - Marco Civil da Internet
summary_short: Establishes principles, user rights and duties for internet use in Brazil. Covers net neutrality, personal data and log retention, intermediary liability for third-party content after court orders, and foreign providers serving Brazilians. In force 60 days after official publication.
summary_long: Law No. 12,965 of 23 April 2014 (Marco Civil da Internet) sets principles, user rights and duties for internet use in Brazil and guides public authorities at all levels (Arts. 1–3). It grants users privacy and communications protections, consent-based control of personal data, and clear contract terms (Art. 7). Network operators must treat traffic equally, allowing discrimination only for technical needs or emergency services, and must disclose traffic management (Art. 9). Connection providers keep connection logs for one year and application providers keep access logs for six months (Arts. 13, 15); other log and data retention is restricted (Arts. 14, 16). Disclosure of records requires prior judicial authorization (Arts. 10, 22–23). Application providers are liable for third-party content only after failing to remove it under a specific court order (Arts. 19–21). Public bodies receive governance, open-standard and e-government guidelines (Arts. 24–28). Breaches of Arts. 10–11 may incur warnings, fines of up to 10% of the Brazilian group's revenue, suspension or prohibition (Art. 12). Foreign providers serving Brazilian users are covered (Art. 11 §2). The law takes effect 60 days after official publication (Art. 32).

title: Portaria Normativa MME nº 129, de 24 de abril de 2026 - Estabelece Diretrizes para as Temporadas de Acesso de que trata o Decreto nº 12.772/2025 (PNAST)
summary_short: Ministerial normative ordinance setting guidelines for Access Seasons under Decree 12.772/2025 (PNAST): ONS registration of agents, capacity calculation, competitive processes with premium bids where requests exceed capacity, and premium use for tariff modicity. Binding on grid agents and the ONS from publication.
summary_long: Portaria Normativa MME nº 129/2026 sets guidelines for the Access Seasons (Temporadas de Acesso) created by Decree 12.772/2025 (PNAST), for permanent access to the national basic transmission grid or increases in contracted use. The ONS runs a registration (Cadastramento) of interested agents and checks admissibility within fifteen days. The ONS calculates remaining capacity at connection points from PAR/PEL reference cases; the methodology note is joint ONS and EPE, and the quantities note is published at least thirty days before each competitive process. Where requested use exceeds capacity, a competitive process ranks bids by the highest premium in R$/kW, paid upfront. Winners and eligible agents receive a Prior Access Diagnosis enabling a CUST, conditioned on a financial guarantee. Non-compliance may lead to loss of allocated capacity, execution of the participation guarantee and exclusion from the two subsequent seasons. Premiums are allocated to reducing transmission charges (EUST). Transitional rules cover generation winners of energy auctions that use grid margin as a selection criterion. The instrument revokes MME Portarias 311/2013 and 24/2014 and takes effect on publication.

title: Medida Provisória nº 1.318, de 17 de setembro de 2025 - institui o Regime Especial de Tributação para Serviços de Datacenter (REDATA)
summary_short: Provisional measure creating the REDATA tax regime for data-center services, including AI training and inference, for Brazilian firms building or expanding data centres. Enrolled firms get suspended federal taxes on IT equipment, converted to zero rate after performance commitments. Effective on publication; Article 11-C from 1 January 2026.
summary_long: MP 1.318/2025 amends Lei 11.196/2005 to create the REDATA special tax regime for data-center services, defined to include cloud computing, high-performance computing, and training and inference of AI models. Legal persons implementing data-center installation or expansion projects in Brazil may obtain habilitação from the federal tax authority; IT-product suppliers may obtain coabilitação. Habilitação requires commitments to: offer at least 10% of processing and storage capacity to the domestic market; meet sustainability criteria; source all electricity from clean or renewable sources; keep Water Usage Effectiveness at or below 0.05 L/kWh, verified annually; and invest 2% of purchased-product value in R&D (substitutable by an additional 10%). Commitments are reduced by 20% in North, Northeast and Centre-West establishments. Suspended PIS/Pasep, Cofins, IPI and import tax on IT equipment convert to zero rate after compliance. Non-compliance triggers recovery with interest and fine; capacity-commitment breach leads to suspension, and cancellation after 180 days bars re-entry for two years. Most provisions apply from publication; the Article 11-C suspensions run from 1 January 2026 for five years.

title: Decreto nº 10.615, de 29 de janeiro de 2021 - Dispõe sobre o PADIS (Lei nº 11.484/2007) e o Programa Brasil Semicondutores (Lei nº 14.968/2024)
summary_short: Decree 10.615/2021 regulates the PADIS semiconductor incentive regime under Law 11.484/2007 for enrolled Brazilian firms: zero or reduced taxes on goods, services and imports, a tax credit tied to R&D spending, R&D investment duties and sanctions. A 2026 amendment adds the Brasil Semicon programme (Law 14.968/2024).
summary_long: Decree 10.615/2021 regulates the PADIS semiconductor and display industry programme under Law 11.484/2007. Chapter I sets federal tax benefits for enrolled firms: zero rates for PIS/Pasep, Cofins and IPI on qualifying goods and services, reduced import duties, and a 100% income-tax reduction on qualifying device sales. A tax credit is calculated on prior-quarter R&D spending, multiplied by 2.62 and capped at 13.10% of the R&D base. The Ministry of Science, Technology and Innovation grants enrolment for listed activities. Enrolled firms must invest at least 5% of gross revenue in R&D and file annual reports and audit opinions. Chapter V sets infractions and sanctions, including fines, suspension, impediment and cancellation. The 2026 amendment adds the Brasil Semicon programme under Law 14.968/2024, a management council and benefit periods to 31 December 2029.

title: Lei nº 11.484, de 31 de maio de 2007 - Incentivos às indústrias de equipamentos para TV Digital e de componentes eletrônicos semicondutores; institui o PADIS e o PATVD
summary_short: Brazilian statute creating PADIS, an incentive programme for semiconductor and display component makers (tax reductions, a minimum R&D investment of 5% of gross revenue, and a financial tax credit), and PATVD for digital-TV equipment (revoked 2024). It also protects integrated-circuit layout topographies. In force from publication, 31 May 2007.
summary_long: Lei 11.484/2007 establishes two industrial-policy programmes and a layout-design IP regime. PADIS (Chapter I) covers legal entities that invest in R&D and carry out listed semiconductor, display, photovoltaic-component and accumulator activities.
