Departments may order rectification and impose warnings, service suspension and fines of 10,000–100,000 RMB, or 100,000–200,000 RMB where health harms result (Arts. 29–30). Effective from 7/15/2026 (Art. 32).

title: 中华人民共和国反网络暴力法（征求意见稿）
summary_short: Draft PRC anti-cyberviolence law, released for public comment on 29 July 2026. Defines cyberviolence; imposes detection, removal, real-name and complaint duties on online service providers; restricts AI-enabled cyberviolence; sets government coordination, court injunctions and penalties. Effective date blank in draft.
summary_long: Draft Anti-Cyberviolence Law (60 articles, seven chapters) published by the Cyberspace Administration of China for public comment on 29 July 2026, with comments due 28 August 2026. It defines cyberviolence as concentrated or continuous online infringement of reputation, honour, privacy, portrait rights or personal information (Art. 2), and applies to such acts within China and to overseas actors targeting China (Art. 3). Chapter 2 imposes duties on online service providers: internal management systems, real-name verification for information-posting and instant-messaging services (Art. 12), AI-assisted and human monitoring, a bar on algorithmic recommendation of risk content, risk labels, self-protection settings, takedown and account restrictions, rumour refutation, and complaint and appeal channels. Large platforms must run rapid-response mechanisms, annual risk assessments and publish annual reports (Art. 21). Chapter 3 assigns coordination to national and local cyberspace authorities alongside public security and other departments. Prohibited conduct includes AI-enabled cyberviolence (Art. 31) and aiding it (Art. 32). Courts may issue personality-right injunctions (Art. 37), public security may issue warning letters to offenders (Art. 40), and prosecutors may bring public-interest suits (Art. 43). Penalties include warnings, fines, business suspension and joint civil liability (Arts. 47-54). The effective date (Art. 60) is left blank.

title: Artificial Intelligence Law of the People’s Republic of China (Draft for Suggestions from Scholars)
summary_short: Draft PRC Artificial Intelligence Law, prepared as a scholars' suggestion draft. It would regulate AI development, provision and use within the PRC and certain activities abroad affecting PRC interests, imposing duties on developers, providers and users, creating oversight bodies, and setting administrative and civil liability. Effective date is blank.
summary_long: The draft covers AI development, provision and use in the PRC, including promotion, user rights, developer and provider duties, supervision and liability. Articles 10–31 promote compute, data sharing, open source, insurance and funding. Articles 32–40 give users a right to know, explanation and refusal of solely AI-based decisions. Articles 41–48 require safety risk assessments, incident reporting, training data quality and AI content identifiers. Articles 50–57 impose registration, a designated protection officer and annual risk assessments on critical AI. Articles 58–68 create oversight departments, a coordination mechanism, a pilot regime and an expert committee. Articles 69–77 add sector rules for state organs, courts, news, medicine, social bots, biometrics, autonomous driving, social credit and AGI. Penalties include rectification, warnings, confiscation of illegal income and, for serious violations, fines up to RMB 50 million or five percent of prior-year turnover (Art. 82). Civil liability, punitive damages and foundation-model liability are addressed (Arts 85–91). Personal use, AI scientific research and free open-source AI are excluded (Art. 95). The effective date is blank (Art. 96).

title: 北京市自动驾驶汽车条例
summary_short: Beijing municipal regulation, in force from 1 April 2025, governing testing, demonstration and road-application pilots of autonomous vehicles in Beijing. It sets approval steps and duties for vehicle makers, pilot operators and data handlers, and fines for unauthorised pilots and maintenance or staffing breaches.
summary_long: Beijing municipal regulation adopted by the 16th Beijing Municipal People's Congress Standing Committee on 31 December 2024, in force from 1 April 2025. It governs innovation, roadside infrastructure, road testing, demonstration applications and road-application pilots of autonomous vehicles in Beijing. Road testing and demonstration applications are reviewed and confirmed by the economic and information technology department; road-application pilots require a safety assessment and a pilot qualification from the transport department. Pilot operators must have safety officers and platform monitoring staff, a safety monitoring platform, and must keep operating records. Vehicle makers must maintain functional safety, cybersecurity and data security capabilities and manage software upgrades. Data rules require risk assessments for important data and breach reporting; cross-border transfers follow national rules. Mandatory insurance applies to tests and pilots. Fines of RMB 30,000 to 100,000 apply to pilots run without consent, and RMB 10,000 to 30,000 to failures to maintain or inspect pilot vehicles or to staff them properly. Traffic violations and accidents are handled under national traffic rules.

title: 北京市发展和改革委员会关于印发进一步加强数据中心项目节能审查若干规定的通知
summary_short: Beijing DRC normative document, in force 4 August 2023, setting energy-review conditions for new and expanded data-centre projects in Beijing using at least 1,000 tce or 5 million kWh a year: PUE caps of 1.3 to 1.15 by energy-use band, storage and renewable-energy rules, monitoring, and differential electricity prices for data centres above PUE 1.4.
summary_long: The Provisions apply to new, expanded or renovated data-centre projects in Beijing with annual energy use of at least 1,000 tonnes of standard coal equivalent or annual electricity use of at least 5 million kWh, including projects whose racks and cooling reach those levels. Data centres must mainly serve the capital's 'four centres' functions and mainly provide computing; storage racks may not exceed 20% of total rack power. Energy reports must contain a renewable-energy plan; projects completed from 2021 are encouraged to raise the renewable share by 10% a year to 100% by 2030, verified annually by a third party commissioned by the energy-review authority. PUE may not exceed 1.3, 1.25, 1.2 or 1.15 depending on annual energy use. Further duties cover natural cooling, waste-heat use, grade-1 efficiency equipment, a ban on new equipment using ozone-depleting substances, reclaimed water, energy and water management systems, and online energy monitoring for projects of 5,000 tce or more. Half the rack power of a developer's closed Beijing data centres can be deducted from a new project's energy use. Projects below 80% rack loading two years after approval must apply for a change. Liability follows the national energy-review measures, with publication of results and credit-system records. Data centres operating above PUE 1.4 pay a surcharge of CNY 0.2 or 0.5 per kWh. The 2021 provisions are repealed.
text_version: Original as issued by notice 京发改规〔2023〕10号 (Jing Fagai Gui [2023] No. 10), dated 2023-07-03; portal status 现行有效 [currently valid] at retrieval

title: 北京市数字经济促进条例
summary_short: Beijing municipal regulation, in force 1 January 2023, promoting the digital economy within the municipal area. It sets rules and support measures for digital infrastructure, data resources and data trading, digital industry and industrial digitalisation, smart-city projects, and digital economy security, addressed to government bodies, enterprises and data handlers.
summary_long: Adopted by the Beijing Municipal People's Congress Standing Committee on 25 November 2022 and in force from 1 January 2023 (Art. 58). It applies to digital economy promotion activities within the Beijing municipal administrative area (Art. 2). It covers digital infrastructure, including information networks, computing infrastructure and support for total-volume control of new data centres (Arts. 9-14); public data catalogues, open data and public data zones (Arts. 16-19); data trading institutions, which must review data sources and parties and keep records (Art. 22); support for digital industries and industrial digitalisation (Arts. 23-36); smart-city projects, including government procurement and opening of public application scenarios (Arts. 37-43); and digital economy security (Arts. 44-49). Data processing entities must establish data governance and compliance systems, protect personal information and report incidents (Art. 48). Platform enterprises must not use data, algorithms or traffic advantages to exclude rivals or discriminate against consumers (Art. 49). Support measures include funds, talent provisions and exemptions or mitigation of liability for good-faith policy exploration (Arts. 51-57). The text sets no fines of its own; it refers to enforcement by competent departments and under other laws.

title: 北京经济技术开发区关于加强数据中心能耗管理的若干措施
summary_short: Management committee measures, effective 2024-03-13, on energy management of data centres in Yizhuang New City (above 50 racks or 250 kW). Links rewards to green power and PUE 1.4, applies differential electricity pricing above the benchmark, caps power use at approved levels, and in principle bars new data centres.
summary_long: Measures issued by the Beijing Economic-Technological Development Area management committee, dated 2024-03-13 and published 2024-04-03, to improve energy and carbon efficiency of data centres in the Yizhuang New City area. They apply to data centres with more than 50 racks or over 250 kW of total rack power, together with their parks and enterprises, including storage, cloud, AI computing, edge and supercomputing facilities. The measures provide for a registry and monitoring through an energy-saving monitoring platform; rewards and recommendations for funding support for data centres that use green electricity, meet a PUE benchmark of 1.4, or convert to intelligent computing centres; public listing of compliant centres; exclusion from infrastructure REITs filings for unauthorised industrial-land use or non-compliant projects; differential electricity pricing for data centres above the benchmark, with the committee determining the subjects; support for relocation to Hebei and Inner Mongolia; a general presumption against new data centres, with economic cooperation agreements for qualifying projects; a cap on electricity use at energy-saving review approvals; and inspections, with penalties under the national energy-saving review measures, publication of results, and reporting to the credit system and joint sanctions for listed seriously dishonest entities.

title: (Trial) Measures for Artificial Intelligence Technology Ethics Management Services (Draft for Public Feedback)
summary_short: Draft trial measures by MIIT and ten other bodies requiring universities, research institutes, medical institutions and firms doing ethically risky AI research and development in China to obtain ethics review by an in-house committee or service center, plus expert re-review for listed activities. Effective date blank.
summary_long: The draft covers AI research, development and similar activities in China that may pose ethical risks to life and health, human dignity, the environment, public order or sustainable development. Units carrying out such activities are responsible; units with the capacity should set up a multidisciplinary AI ethics committee. Provincial authorities and State Council departments may set up ethics service centers that review on commission. Activity leaders apply with a plan, an ethics risk assessment and a commitment letter. Committees choose a general, simplified or emergency procedure, review fairness, controllability, transparency and explainability, traceability and risk-benefit, decide within 30 days, and conduct follow-up review at most every 12 months, with power to suspend or terminate activities. Activities on an annexed list (human-machine fusion systems affecting behaviour or health, algorithms able to mobilise public opinion, highly autonomous automated decision systems in safety or health settings) also need expert re-review by the competent authority, unless an existing filing or approval regime already covers ethics. Units register committees and listed activities on a national platform and file annual reports. Violations are penalised under the Science and Technology Progress Law and other laws. The draft also sets out government support measures.
text_version: Public consultation draft (公开征求意见稿), notice dated 2025-08-22; comments due 2025-09-22

title: 促进和规范数据跨境流动规定 (Provisions on Promoting and Regulating Cross-Border Data Flows)
summary_short: Chinese CAC rules, in force from promulgation, that set when data processors must pass a national security assessment, sign a standard contract or obtain certification before providing data abroad, and exempt listed low-risk transfers from those steps.
summary_long: Order No. 16 of the Cyberspace Administration of China, adopted at the CAC's 2023 26th office meeting and in force from its publication. It governs outbound provision of data by data processors. Exemptions (Arts. 2-6) cover data that is neither personal information nor important data, transfers in international trade, cross-border transport and academic cooperation, foreign-collected data processed in China, transfers needed for contracts with individuals, cross-border HR management and emergencies, and transfers by non-CIIO processors of personal information of fewer than 100,000 people (excluding sensitive data) cumulatively since 1 January. A security assessment through the provincial CAC is required for CIIO operators transferring personal information or important data, and for other processors transferring important data or personal information of 1 million or more people, or sensitive personal information of 10,000 or more (Art. 7). Non-CIIO processors transferring data of 100,000 to under 1 million people, or under 10,000 sensitive-data subjects, must sign a standard contract or obtain personal information protection certification (Art. 8). Assessment results are valid for three years, extendable by three years on application (Art. 9). Processors must also meet consent, notice and impact assessment duties (Art. 10), data security and incident reporting duties (Art. 11), and local CAC supervision (Art. 12). Free trade zones may set negative lists subject to provincial approval and filing (Art. 6). The rules prevail over conflicting 2022 and 2023 measures (Art. 13).

title: 全国人民代表大会常务委员会关于修改《中华人民共和国网络安全法》的决定 (NPCSC Decision on Amending the Cybersecurity Law)
summary_short: Amends China's Cybersecurity Law, effective 1 January 2026. Adds general principles and a provision on state support for AI research and infrastructure, adds personal-information processing duties, and revises penalties for network operators, critical information infrastructure operators, and product sellers, plus foreign actors harming cybersecurity.
summary_long: NPC Standing Committee decision adopted 28 October 2025, effective 1 January 2026, amending the Cybersecurity Law. It adds Art. 3 (Party leadership, overall national security concept, network power). New Art. 20 directs state support for AI basic research, key algorithms, training-data and computing infrastructure, AI ethics norms, risk monitoring and assessment, safety supervision, AI application, and AI use in cybersecurity management. New paragraph in Art. 42 requires network operators processing personal information to comply with the Cybersecurity Law, Civil Code and Personal Information Protection Law. Renumbers and rewrites the penalty provisions (Arts. 61-77): graded fines for breaching network security protection duties of network operators and critical information infrastructure operators; new Art. 63 penalising sale of uncertified critical network equipment and security products; Art. 67 fines of one to ten times procurement amount for critical infrastructure operators using unreviewed network products; higher fines for publishing prohibited information; cross-reference to other laws for personal information and cross-border data breaches; a mitigation clause (Art. 73); and Art. 77 liability and asset-freezing measures for overseas actors endangering China's cybersecurity.

title: 国家网络安全事件报告管理办法
summary_short: Requires network operators in China to report cybersecurity incidents to designated authorities within deadlines of 1 to 4 hours for initial reports, depending on operator type and incident grade. Provides an incident classification guide and requires a post-incident summary report within 30 days. Effective 1 November 2025.
summary_long: Issued by the Cyberspace Administration of China on 11 September 2025, in force from 1 November 2025 (Art. 14). Applies to network owners, managers and service providers in China (Arts. 2, 12). Operators must classify incidents under the attached Guide and report larger-grade or higher incidents: critical information infrastructure operators to the protection authority and public security within 1 hour; central state organs to their cyberspace bodies within 2 hours; other operators to the provincial cyberspace authority within 4 hours; major incidents are escalated to the national authority within 30 minutes or 1 hour (Art. 4). Operators must require contracted service providers to report incidents (Art. 5). Reports must cover specified content, including ransom details for ransomware, with supplementary reports as facts emerge (Art. 7). A post-incident summary report is due within 30 days (Art. 8). Non-reporting is penalised under other laws; aggravated penalties apply where late, missed, false or concealed reports cause serious harm (Art. 10). Operators with reasonable protective measures may receive lighter treatment (Art. 11). The Guide sets four grades with quantitative criteria.

title: 数据出境安全评估办法 (Measures for Security Assessment of Outbound Data Transfers)
summary_short: Sets rules for security assessment of outbound transfers of important data and personal information by data processors in China: declaration thresholds, self-assessment, contract terms, review timelines and two-year validity. Effective 1 September 2022.
summary_long: Issued by the Cyberspace Administration of China as Order No. 11 and effective 1 September 2022, the Measures govern security assessment of outbound transfers of important data and personal information collected and generated in China. Processors must declare an assessment to the national authority, through provincial authorities, when exporting important data, when critical information infrastructure operators or processors of over one million people's personal information export personal information, or when cumulative exports since 1 January of the prior year reach 100,000 people's personal information or 10,000 people's sensitive personal information. Processors must first self-assess legality, risks and recipient safeguards, and submit a self-assessment report, the declaration form and the contract with the recipient. The national authority completes review within 45 working days of written acceptance, extendable with notice. Review results may be contested by a reconsideration request within 15 working days, whose result is final. A passed result is valid for two years; re-declaration is required after specified changes or 60 working days before expiry. Contracts must set out data security duties, limits on onward transfer and remedies. The authority may order termination of approved transfers that no longer meet requirements. Violations may be reported; liability is handled under the Cybersecurity, Data Security and Personal Information Protection laws, with criminal liability where applicable. Transfers under way before the effective date must be rectified within six months.

title: 互联网信息服务深度合成管理规定 (Provisions on the Administration of Deep Synthesis Internet Information Services)
summary_short: Governs providers, technical supporters and users of internet services that apply deep synthesis technology to generate or edit text, voice, images, video or virtual scenes. Imposes content review, real-name verification, labelling and filing duties; effective 10 January 2023.
summary_long: Governs providers, technical supporters and users of internet services that apply deep synthesis technology to generate or edit text, voice, images, video or virtual scenes (Arts. 2, 23). The state internet information department coordinates oversight, with telecommunications and public security departments and local counterparts acting within their duties (Art. 3). Users may not produce prohibited or fake news content (Art. 6). Providers must run management systems, verify users' real identity, review inputs and outputs, handle complaints and dispel rumours (Arts. 7–12). App stores must check security assessments and filings (Art. 13). Providers must manage training data, obtain individual consent for biometric editing functions, review algorithms, and security-assess biometric or sensitive-content tools (Arts. 14–15). Synthetic content must carry technical symbols and, for listed services, conspicuous labels; deleting labels is prohibited (Arts. 16–18). Services with public-opinion or mobilisation capacity must file and assess new products (Arts. 19–20). Authorities may inspect and request suspension of services; violations are punished under other laws, with criminal liability where a crime is constituted (Arts. 21–22). Effective 10 January 2023 (Art. 25).

title: 数字虚拟人信息服务管理办法（征求意见稿）
summary_short: Comment draft (3 April 2026) of CAC measures governing digital virtual human information services offered to the public in mainland China. Sets consent, likeness, minors, content, labelling, filing and complaint duties for providers, technical supporters and users, with penalties under Art. 24. The effective date is blank in the draft.
summary_long: Comment draft (published 3 April 2026) of CAC measures on digital virtual human information services offered to the public within mainland China (Art. 2). Defines digital virtual humans and real-person-driven ones (Art. 25). CAC coordinates; sectoral and local authorities supervise within their remits (Art. 3). Requires separate consent and clear notice for using sensitive personal information for modelling or image generation, with guardian consent for users under 14 (Art. 7). Bars identifiable likenesses of specific persons without their consent (Art. 8). Prohibits inducing minors' addiction and virtual intimate relationships with minors (Art. 10). Lists prohibited content (Art. 11) and requires a persistent 'digital human' label where the service is shown (Art. 13). Providers must sign service agreements with technical supporters and users (Art. 16) and run complaint channels (Art. 20). Services with public-opinion or social-mobilisation capacity must make algorithm filings and security assessments (Arts. 21-22). Government and judicial uses require human review and user choice (Art. 19). Penalties include warnings, criticism and rectification orders; service suspension, which may be combined with fines of 10,000 to 100,000 yuan, and fines of 100,000 to 200,000 yuan where harm to life or health results (Art. 24). The effective date is blank (Art. 27).
text_version: CAC consultation draft (征求意见稿), published 2026-04-03

title: 中华人民共和国数据安全法 (Data Security Law of the PRC)
summary_short: Sets rules for data processing and data security in China: data classification, risk monitoring, incident response, a national security review, export controls, and limits on cross-border transfer of important data and on foreign data requests. Penalties apply from 1 September 2021.
summary_long: Governs data processing (collection, storage, use, processing, transmission, provision, disclosure) and data security in mainland China, and reaches processing outside China that harms Chinese national security, public interest or the rights of citizens and organisations. Establishes a central national security coordination mechanism and sectoral and local data regulators. Requires data classification and grading, with catalogues of important data and stricter rules for core data; provides for risk assessment, reporting, incident response and a national security review of data processing. Processors must maintain full-process data security management, training and technical measures; processors of important data must designate a responsible person and submit periodic risk assessment reports. Imposes export controls on certain controlled items, restricts transfer of important data abroad and disclosure of stored data to foreign judicial or law-enforcement bodies, regulates data trading intermediaries, requires administrative licences where other laws require them, and sets rules for government data and open government data. Penalties include warnings, fines (for basic violations 50,000 to 500,000 yuan, higher in serious cases), suspension of business, revocation of licences and civil or criminal liability. Takes effect 1 September 2021.

title: 中华人民共和国两用物项出口管制条例 (Regulations of the PRC on Export Control of Dual-Use Items)
summary_short: The State Council regulation controls exports of dual-use items (goods, technology, services and related data) through licensing, end-user and end-use management, and control and watch lists, with penalties for violations. It applies from 1 December 2024 and repeals four earlier export control regulations.
summary_long: Issued as State Council Decree No. 792 (adopted 18 September 2024, promulgated 30 September 2024, effective 1 December 2024), the regulation implements the Export Control Law for dual-use items: goods, technology, services and related data with civil uses and military or weapons-of-mass-destruction relevance. Chapter 2 covers policy, a dual-use item list, temporary controls on items outside the list (each for up to two years), and prohibitions on specific items or destinations. Chapter 3 requires licences for listed items: single licences (valid up to one year), general licences (valid up to three years, for exporters with an internal compliance system and export record) or registration-based export certificates. Single-licence applications are decided within 45 working days, and changes to non-critical elements within 20 working days. Exports must be presented to customs with the licence. Chapter 3 also covers end-user and end-use statements and the watch list and control list of importers and end users, against which transactions may be banned or restricted. Chapter 4 sets supervision and inspection powers. Chapter 5 provides for warnings, confiscation, fines and criminal liability. Chapter 6 covers transit, re-export and overseas-made items containing Chinese-origin items, and repeals four earlier regulations on nuclear, missile, biological and chemical dual-use export controls.

title: 广州市人工智能发展促进条例（草案修改稿·征求意见稿）
summary_short: Draft revision for public comment of the Guangzhou AI development promotion regulation. It applies within Guangzhou's administrative area, promotes AI infrastructure, data, procurement, funding and talent support, prohibits listed AI conduct, and imposes civil liability for resulting harm. The effective date is blank.
summary_long: This draft revision of the Guangzhou AI development promotion regulation applies to AI factor support, application, industrial development and security activities within Guangzhou's administrative area. It establishes a municipal AI leading group and expert committee, and tasks development, science, industry, data and other departments with computing infrastructure, a city-wide computing coordination platform, open and authorised public data resources, high-quality datasets, testbeds and application scenario opening. Government procurement of listed AI products and services is encouraged, and funding, land, startup investment, talent and industrial park support are provided. Article 18 sets inclusive, tiered supervision for new AI technologies and products. Article 19 prohibits AI research and application activities that lack measures against discriminatory outcomes, that fail to implement content review, labelling or algorithm review and cause harmful AI-generated false information, that use algorithms for price discrimination or consumer fraud, or that lack safety intervention and accountability mechanisms in autonomous driving and intelligent medical systems causing harm. Other penalties are left to the cited laws and regulations, and harm may give rise to civil liability. Article 21 leaves the effective date blank..
text_version: revised draft for comment (草案修改稿·征求意见稿) published 2026-08-17, comments until 2026-09-18

title: Regulations of Shenzhen Special Economic Zone on Promoting the Artificial Intelligence Industry
summary_short: Regulations of Shenzhen Special Economic Zone promoting the AI industry, in force 1 November 2022. They set municipal coordination and promotion measures for research, infrastructure, data and applications, establish an AI ethics committee, require risk-based supervision, and prohibit listed conduct by AI research and application organisations.
summary_long: The Regulations, adopted by the Standing Committee of the 7th Shenzhen Municipal People's Congress on 30 August 2022 and in force from 1 November 2022, promote the AI industry in Shenzhen Municipality and set governance rules for AI research and application. The municipal competent industry authorities implement and supervise the AI industry within the municipal administrative area. Chapters II to V set promotional measures, including support for basic research and funding, public data resources and data sharing, AI data centres subject to higher energy efficiency standards, testing and certification platforms, application scenarios, and talent and investment support. Article 44 allows low-risk AI products without national or local standards to be piloted. Article 65 establishes a municipal AI ethics committee. Article 66 requires classified supervision: high-risk applications face pre-process evaluation and risk warning, while medium- and low-risk applications face pre-process disclosure and post-process tracking. Article 71 requires algorithms used in public decision-making to be explained to the public. Article 72 requires ethical safety reviews and risk assessments and prohibits, among other acts, endangering national security or public interests, infringing privacy, discriminating against users, and price discrimination based on user habits. Violations are to be punished or investigated under the Civil Code and related laws.

title: 深圳市打造人工智能先锋城市的若干措施
summary_short: Shenzhen municipal measures issued 18 Dec 2024 (valid 2 years) to support AI development: vouchers and grants for compute, models, corpora and applications, plus R&D, incubation and talent support for AI firms and research bodies.
summary_long: Issued by the Shenzhen Municipal Bureau of Industry and Information Technology (深工信规〔2024〕13号) after municipal government approval, effective 18 December 2024 for two years. The measures set out funding and in-kind support for AI in Shenzhen in five parts. Part one provides compute-service discounts and 'training vouchers' (up to 500 million yuan a year) covering up to 50% of contract value for model training, plus 'corpus vouchers' funding purchases of non-affiliated corpora. Part two offers 'model vouchers' (up to 100 million yuan a year) for use of filed generative AI models, grants for industry application demonstrations, opening of government application scenarios, and subsidies for AI hardware and software. Part three funds basic research and technology projects, open-source and ecosystem centres, public technology platforms and key laboratories. Part four provides rent-free incubator space, park awards, talent start-up grants, financing subsidies and industry events. Part five bars double-claiming against other municipal incentives, caps funding by annual totals, limits cumulative project funding to audited investment where national or provincial support exists, and allows adjustment to implementing rules. Responsibilities are assigned to named municipal bureaus.
text_version: as issued 2024-12-18 (深工信规〔2024〕13号), Shenzhen Government Gazette 2024 No. 42

title: 深圳经济特区数据条例
summary_short: Shenzhen Special Economic Zone regulation, effective 1 January 2022, governing personal data processing, public data sharing and opening, the data market and data security, with administrative fines and civil liability for violations.
summary_long: The regulation governs data processing in the Shenzhen Special Economic Zone from 1 January 2022. Chapter 2 sets personal data rules: notice and consent, with explicit consent for sensitive personal data, biometric data and data of children under 14; minimisation; withdrawal of consent; and limits on user profiling. Chapter 3 provides for sharing public data as the principle, a municipal big data centre, and classification of public data as unconditionally open, conditionally open or not open. Chapter 4 promotes a data factor market and trading platforms, and prohibits illegal acquisition of other market actors' data, discriminatory treatment through data analysis, and monopolistic conduct. Chapter 5 requires data classification, security measures, incident response, periodic risk assessments for sensitive or important data, and security assessment before cross-border provision of personal or important data. Chapter 6 refers personal data violations to personal information protection law and sets administrative fines, corrective orders and civil liability.

title: 深圳经济特区智能网联汽车管理条例
summary_short: Shenzhen regulation on intelligent connected vehicles covering road testing and demonstration applications, product admission, registration, use management, infrastructure, network security, data protection and liability. Applies within the Shenzhen Special Economic Zone from 1 August 2022, as amended with effect from 1 July 2026.
summary_long: The regulation, adopted by the Shenzhen Municipal People's Congress Standing Committee on 23 June 2022 and effective 1 August 2022 (Art. 64), governs intelligent connected vehicles in the Shenzhen Special Economic Zone. A 2026 decision amended it with effect from 1 July 2026; this text is the consolidated version reprinted after that amendment. Vehicles are defined by three automation levels (conditional, high and full driving automation). Road testing and demonstration applications require filing, approval and temporary plates. Vehicles must be on the municipal product catalogue to be sold and on the registration system before road use, and must connect to a government supervisory platform and upload operating-safety data. Manufacturers must report safety defects and recall vehicles. Driver, owner and manager duties depend on automation level, and event data must be recorded for at least 90 seconds and stored for at least 30 days. Network security duties, a requirement to store data on servers within China with no outbound transfer without approval, and a ban on unlawful collection of user information apply. Accident liability is allocated by automation level. Penalties include seizure and fines of 100,000 to 500,000 yuan for unauthorised road testing.
text_version: as amended 2026-05-25, republished in Shenzhen Government Gazette 2026 No. 19, in force 2026-07-01

title: 生成式人工智能服务管理暂行办法 (Interim Measures for the Management of Generative Artificial Intelligence Services)
summary_short: Departmental rules of the CAC and six other ministries, in force 15 August 2023, governing generative AI services offered to the public in mainland China: content, training-data, data-labelling, personal-information, content-labelling and complaint duties for providers, plus security assessment and algorithm filing for services with public-opinion attributes.
summary_long: The Interim Measures apply to services that use generative AI to provide text, images, audio, video and other content to the public within the PRC. They do not apply to organisations that develop or use the technology without offering it to the domestic public, and sector-specific rules on news publishing, film and television, and literary and artistic creation take precedence. Providers and users must observe content rules (core socialist values, no prohibited content), take measures against discrimination, respect intellectual property, competition rules and personal rights, and improve transparency, accuracy and reliability. Providers must use lawful data and foundation models for training, obtain consent for personal information, improve training-data quality, set rules for data labelling, sign service agreements with users, disclose intended users and uses, guard minors against over-reliance, protect user inputs, label generated content under the deep synthesis provisions, act on illegal content and users, and run complaint channels. Services with public-opinion attributes or social mobilisation capacity need a security assessment and an algorithm filing. Breaches are punished under the Cybersecurity, Data Security, Personal Information Protection and Science and Technology Progress laws. Where those laws are silent, authorities issue warnings, public criticism and rectification orders, and can suspend the service. The CAC can have non-compliant services from outside the PRC dealt with by technical measures.
text_version: original as promulgated by Order No. 15 of seven departments (dated 2023-07-10; posted on cac.gov.cn 2023-07-13)

title: 甘肃省人民政府办公厅印发关于支持全国一体化算力网络国家枢纽节点（甘肃）建设运营若干措施的通知
summary_short: Gansu measures (Gan Zheng Ban Fa [2022] No. 103) supporting the Gansu hub of the national integrated computing network. Directs new large data centres in principle to the Qingyang cluster; provides land, electricity, energy-quota, tax, finance and talent support; requires monitoring; bans crypto mining in data centres. Dated 28 August 2022.
summary_long: Notice of the Gansu Provincial People's Government General Office (Gan Zheng Ban Fa [2022] No. 103), dated 28 August 2022 and published 20 September 2022, setting out measures to support construction and operation of the Gansu hub of the national integrated computing network. Part I covers factors: new large data centres are to be located in the Qingyang cluster in principle, and local governments may not grant land or tax preferences for data centres built outside it; older, small or inefficient facilities are to be retrofitted to electricity-use efficiency of 1.5 or below by 2025; land, electricity and energy-quota arrangements are set, including exemption from demand-charge fees for big-data firms until end-2025. Part II covers talent training and support. Part III covers funding, tax and finance: special-fund support, a 15% corporate income tax rate for qualifying Qingyang firms, a 50% reduction of listed local taxes for 2022-2024, and credit support. Part IV covers investment attraction, approval streamlining and a ban on discriminatory pricing by telecom operators. Part V covers regulation: a monitoring platform for data-centre energy use, a ban on crypto mining in data centres, responsibility commitments, and a two-year inclusive supervision period for new business types.

title: 互联网信息服务管理办法（修订草案征求意见稿）
summary_short: Draft revision of China's Internet Information Service Management Measures (2026 consultation text). Applies to internet information services in China and sets licensing, filing, content and user-account duties, plus platform, algorithm and AI-service rules; the effective date is left blank in the draft.
summary_long: Draft revision of China's Internet Information Service Management Measures (consultation text, 3 July 2026): six chapters, 94 articles, drafted by CAC with MIIT and MPS. It covers internet information services in China and, under Art. 92, overseas providers serving China. Chapter 2 requires approval from the telecommunications authority (Art. 8-9). Chapter 3 requires filing within 30 days of network connection (Art. 16) and real-name verification (Art. 19), sets content prohibitions (Art. 24-25), removal and reporting duties (Art. 27), anti-rumour measures (Art. 31), minors' protection (Art. 35) and six-month log retention (Art. 39). Section 2 imposes platform duties, including published platform rules, account credit systems, and extra obligations for large platforms (Art. 54). Section 3 covers intelligent information services: lawful training data (Art. 59), labelling of AI-generated content (Art. 60), algorithm recommendation controls (Art. 61), gig-worker algorithm rules (Art. 62) and agent services (Art. 63). Chapter 5 provides warnings, fines, suspension, closure, licence revocation and civil or criminal liability. The effective date (Art. 94) is blank; comments close 2 August 2026.

title: 江苏省人工智能产业发展促进条例（草案）
summary_short: Draft Jiangsu provincial regulation to promote the AI industry in Jiangsu. It covers government coordination, public data and high-quality datasets, computing infrastructure and data-centre power coordination, sector applications, safety and filing duties for AI service providers, ethics committees, and state support. The effective date is blank in the draft.
summary_long: The draft regulation applies to activities that promote the AI industry within Jiangsu Province (Art. 2). Provincial and municipal governments and designated departments coordinate industry development, with the data authority responsible for public data resources and high-quality datasets (Arts. 4-5, 11-12). It provides for unified computing infrastructure and scheduling, a public computing-sharing mechanism, and coordination between data-centre power use and grid operators, with encouragement of green power purchases (Arts. 14-16). It promotes AI in manufacturing, agriculture, medicine, transport, education, public services and government governance (Arts. 35-45). AI service providers must complete security assessments and filings under national rules and label AI-generated content (Art. 47). Research and development entities must establish ethics committees (Art. 49). The regulation allows sandbox and inclusive supervision (Art. 46), and provides for special funds, computing and token vouchers, and financing support (Arts. 52-53). Penalties are left to existing law, and officials are liable for dereliction of duty (Art. 62). The effective date is blank (Art. 63).
text_version: draft (草案) as published for public comment 2026-07-31 (comment period to 2026-08-30), after first reading 2026-07-29

title: 南京市人工智能产业发展和创新应用促进条例（草案）
summary_short: Draft Nanjing municipal regulation on AI industry development and application. It sets coordination mechanisms, government support for R&D, industry, talent and funds, public-sector AI use and procurement, data and compute support, sandbox pilots, and conduct rules for AI developers and providers. Effective date is unspecified (202X).
summary_long: Draft municipal regulation (征求意见稿) applying to AI science and technology innovation, industry development, application integration and safety governance within Nanjing's administrative area (Art. 3). Chapters cover: a city coordination mechanism and an expert advisory committee (Arts. 5, 7); support for basic research, key technology, platforms and talent (Arts. 11-15, 48); industry development priorities, enterprise cultivation including OPC enterprises, and platform and chain-leader enterprises (Arts. 16-27); sectoral application duties for manufacturing, agriculture, energy, consumption, education, healthcare, transport and government services (Arts. 28-40); preferential public procurement of safe and reliable AI products (Art. 29); factor support for data, computing power and algorithms (Arts. 41-44); financial support, funds and insurance (Arts. 45-47); and safety governance. Safety governance includes government AI safety supervision (Art. 53), a sandbox mechanism allowing limited trial operation with suspension or termination on major risk (Art. 54), a list of prohibited AI products and conduct, including price discrimination and deepfake misuse (Art. 55), a ban on abuse of dominance by chain-leader and platform enterprises (Art. 56), algorithmic fairness assessment and explanation duties in public management, healthcare, finance and judicial areas (Art. 57), and ethics review (Art. 58). The draft sets no fines or penalty amounts, and its effective date is blank (Art. 59).
text_version: consultation draft (征求意见稿) published 2026-04-21 by Nanjing Municipal Bureau of Industry and IT (59 articles)

title: 大型个人信息处理者个人信息保护规定（征求意见稿）
summary_short: Draft CAC measures for designated large personal information handlers: designation criteria (including processing data of 10 million or more individuals), localisation and cross-border transfer duties, automated-decision and minors' safeguards, impact assessments, audits, reporting and an external-majority supervisory committee. Effective date blank; comments close 7 Sept 2026.
summary_long: The draft would let the CAC and other personal-information authorities designate large personal information handlers. Designation considers processing data of 10 million or more individuals, providing important network services or multi-business operations involving personal information, and impact on national security, the economy, social stability or public health and safety (Art. 2-3). Chapter 2 sets processing duties: transparent rules, separate consent for transfers, public disclosure, sensitive data and sharing, guardian consent for under-14s, domestic storage in designated data centres (Art. 13-14), an option to switch off personalised push, data portability within 30 working days, and cross-border transfers under security assessment, standard contract or certification (Art. 20). Chapter 3 requires a responsible officer, internal systems, annual social responsibility reports, pre-launch impact assessments for automated-decision and sensitive-data products, minors' compliance audits, and audits every two years. Chapter 4 requires a supervisory committee of at least seven members, two-thirds external, formed within six months of designation. Chapter 5 provides for filings, inspections, interviews, rectification and committee dissolution, and refers penalties to the PIPL and other laws. The effective date is blank (Art. 50).

title: 国务院关于保障未成年人健康安全使用网络的规定（征求意见稿）
summary_short: Draft State Council regulation on minors' safe internet use. Applies to network services offered to minors in China, smart terminal makers and app distributors. Bars listed services to minors, requires a minors' mode for under-16 users, mandates user age identification, filing with regulators and administrative penalties. Effective date left blank in the draft.
summary_long: The draft State Council regulation would apply to network services provided to minors in China, to manufacturers of smart terminal products, and to app distribution platforms (Art. 2). It sets a principle of acting in minors' best interest and provides for minors' mode (Art. 3). It bars providers from offering listed services to minors, including stranger social networking, virtual intimate relationships, and live-streaming publishing for those under sixteen, with exceptions (Art. 4). Services listed in Art. 5, including social networking, games, and AI services that may affect minors' cognition, must be offered through a minors' mode to users under sixteen. Providers must identify minor users (Art. 6), manage harmful content (Art. 7), review recommendation algorithms and avoid models that induce emotional dependence or excessive spending (Art. 8), and offer appeal channels (Art. 9). Terminal makers and app distributors must support minors' mode and review applications (Art. 10). Minors' mode settings must be filed with provincial network authorities, with large platforms filing through them with the national authority (Art. 12). Penalties include warnings, confiscation, fines, suspension and closure (Arts. 18 to 20). Civil and criminal liability is preserved (Art. 21). The effective date is left blank.

title: 商务部 海关总署公告2023年第23号 关于对镓、锗相关物项实施出口管制的公告 (MOFCOM/GAC Announcement No. 23 of 2023 on export controls on gallium- and germanium-related items)
summary_short: Requires MOFCOM export licences for listed gallium- and germanium-related items, including metals, compounds and wafers, from 1 August 2023. Exporters apply through provincial commerce authorities; customs clears shipments against the licence.
summary_long: Joint announcement of the Ministry of Commerce (MOFCOM) and General Administration of Customs (GAC), dated 3 July 2023 and issued with State Council approval under the Export Control Law, Foreign Trade Law and Customs Law. Item 1 prohibits export without a licence of listed gallium-related items (metallic gallium, gallium nitride, gallium oxide, gallium arsenide and others) and germanium-related items (metallic germanium, germanium ingots, germanium dioxide, germanium tetrachloride and others). Item 2 lists application documents, filed through provincial commerce authorities. Item 3 requires MOFCOM to review and decide within statutory time limits, with State Council approval for items of major national-security impact. Items 4 to 6 cover licence issuance, licensing procedures under a 2005 MOFCOM/GAC order, and customs clearance against the licence. Item 7 refers unlicensed or excess exports to administrative penalties and criminal liability under other laws. Item 8 sets entry into force on 1 August 2023.

title: 商务部公告2024年第46号 关于加强相关两用物项对美国出口管制的公告 (MOFCOM Announcement No. 46 of 2024 on strengthening export controls of dual-use items to the United States)
summary_short: Bans dual-use item exports to US military users or uses, in principle refuses licences for gallium, germanium, antimony and superhard-material items to the US, and tightens end-user review for graphite exports to the US. Effective on publication, 3 December 2024.
summary_long: MOFCOM Announcement No. 46 of 2024, issued by the Ministry of Commerce on 3 December 2024 under the Export Control Law and other laws, strengthens export controls on dual-use items destined for the United States. Item one prohibits exports of dual-use items to US military end users or for military uses. Item two provides that licences will in principle not be granted for dual-use gallium, germanium, antimony and superhard-material items exported to the US, and applies stricter end-user and end-use review to graphite dual-use items exported to the US. The closing unnumbered paragraph states that organisations and individuals of any country or region who, in breach of these rules, transfer or supply Chinese-origin dual-use items to US organisations or individuals will be subject to legal liability under law. The announcement takes effect on publication. It is not specific to AI, and it sets no numeric thresholds, compliance deadlines or penalty amounts.

title: 商务部 海关总署公告2025年第18号 公布对部分中重稀土相关物项实施出口管制的决定 (MOFCOM/GAC Announcement No. 18 of 2025 on export controls on certain medium and heavy rare earth items)
summary_short: Joint MOFCOM and GAC announcement (4 April 2025) placing export controls on listed medium and heavy rare earth items: samarium, gadolinium, terbium, dysprosium, lutetium, scandium and yttrium. Exporters need MOFCOM licences and must flag controlled items at customs. Takes effect on publication.
summary_long: Joint announcement of the Ministry of Commerce and the General Administration of Customs, dated 4 April 2025, issued with State Council approval. It places export controls on listed items relating to seven medium and heavy rare earths: samarium, gadolinium, terbium, dysprosium, lutetium, scandium and yttrium. Covered items include metals, alloys and targets (control codes 1C902.a to 1C908.a), oxides and mixtures (.b), and compounds and mixtures (.c). Samarium-cobalt and terbium- and dysprosium-containing NdFeB permanent magnets are included. Explanatory notes state that alloys and targets include forms such as ingots, bars, powders and sheets, and that oxides and compounds include, but are not limited to, powder forms. Reference customs codes are listed for each item. Exporters must apply to the State Council commerce authority for a licence under the Export Control Law and the Dual-Use Items Export Control Regulations. Exporters must identify controlled items and state at customs declaration whether goods are controlled, giving the dual-use control code where applicable. If customs doubts declared information, it may query the declaration, and goods are not released during the query. The announcement takes effect on the date of publication and states that the dual-use items control list is updated at the same time.

title: 商务部公告2025年第61号 公布对境外相关稀土物项实施出口管制的决定 (MOFCOM Announcement No. 61 of 2025 on export controls on relevant overseas rare earth items)
summary_short: MOFCOM Announcement No. 61 (2025), issued with State Council approval under the Export Control Law and dual-use export regulations, requires export licences for rare-earth-related dual-use items, including foreign-made items with a 0.1% or greater Chinese-origin value share. Parts apply from 9 October 2025 and 1 December 2025.
summary_long: The announcement, issued by the Ministry of Commerce (MOFCOM) with State Council approval under the Export Control Law and the dual-use items export control regulations, sets export controls on rare-earth-related dual-use items for foreign organisations and individuals referred to as foreign specific exporters, and for domestic exporters. Export licences from MOFCOM are required before exporting Annex 1 items that are foreign-made items containing or integrating Chinese-origin Annex 1 Part 1 items at a value share of 0.1% or more, Annex 1 items produced abroad using Chinese rare-earth mining, smelting, magnet or recycling technologies, or Chinese-origin Annex 1 items. Applications for military end users, and for importers and end users on control or watch lists (including subsidiaries at 50% or more ownership), are in principle refused, as are applications for weapons of mass destruction, terrorism or military end uses. Applications for end uses involving 14nm-and-below logic chips, 256-layer-and-above memory chips, related production equipment and materials, or AI research with potential military use are reviewed case by case. Humanitarian emergency exports are exempt from licensing if reported to MOFCOM within 10 working days. Domestic exporters must report final destinations and issue compliance notices, and overseas exporters must pass compliance notices to downstream recipients. Clauses (1) and (2) of point one take effect on 1 December 2025; clause (3) takes effect on publication, 9 October 2025.

title: 商务部、海关总署公告2025年第70号 公布暂停实施商务部、海关总署公告2025年第55号、56号、57号、58号及商务部公告2025年第61号、62号的决定 (MOFCOM/GAC Announcement No. 70 of 2025 suspending Announcements 55–58, 61, 62)
summary_short: Suspends, from the date of issue until 10 November 2026, the implementation of MOFCOM/GAC Announcements No. 55, 56, 57 and 58 of 2025 and MOFCOM Announcements No. 61 and 62 of 2025. The text does not describe what those announcements regulate.
summary_long: Joint announcement No. 70 of 2025 by the Ministry of Commerce (MOFCOM) and the General Administration of Customs (GAC), dated 7 November 2025, suspending the implementation of MOFCOM/GAC Announcements No. 55, 56, 57 and 58 and MOFCOM Announcements No. 61 and 62 (all 2025). The single operative sentence states that, with approval, the listed announcements are suspended from the date of issue to 10 November 2026. The document has no article structure. It does not describe the content of the suspended announcements, the parties they regulate, their thresholds, penalties or definitions, or what takes effect when the suspension ends. The domain classification (chips_export_controls) is provisional: the text itself does not state a subject-matter domain, and it contains no AI-specific provision.

title: 网络数据安全管理条例 (Regulations on Network Data Security Management)
summary_short: Regulation of the State Council (Decree No. 790) governing network data processing in China, applying from 1 January 2025. It sets data-security duties for network data processors, personal information rules, important data risk assessments, cross-border transfer conditions, and platform obligations, enforced by competent authorities.
summary_long: The Regulations, adopted by the State Council on 30 August 2024 and applying from 1 January 2025, govern network data processing and its security supervision within the PRC, and extend to processing outside China of personal information of PRC natural persons in cases meeting Personal Information Protection Law conditions. Network data processors must adopt technical and management measures, report security incidents, and bear responsibility for data security, including when entrusting or sharing processing. For personal information, the text sets consent rules (separate consent for sensitive information, parental consent for under-14s), notice and rights-handling duties, deletion and portability, and periodic compliance audits. Processors of important data must designate security managers, conduct annual risk assessments and report to authorities; catalogues are compiled by the national coordination mechanism and by regional and sectoral authorities. Outbound transfers require a CAC security assessment, certification or a standard contract, subject to listed exceptions. Large online platforms (50 million registered or 10 million monthly active users) must manage third-party providers, verify apps, offer opt-outs from automated push recommendations, publish social responsibility reports, and avoid specified data misuse. Generative AI service providers must manage training data security. Competent authorities supervise compliance, may inspect and require service suspension, and violations carry administrative fines and possible criminal liability.

title: 内蒙古自治区人民政府办公厅关于支持内蒙古和林格尔集群绿色算力产业发展的若干意见
summary_short: Inner Mongolia government office opinions (June 2024, valid three years) supporting green computing in the Horinger data center cluster. They set siting rules for large data centres, electricity and green-power measures, network and computing-platform rewards, PUE limits, and innovation and talent support.
summary_long: These government office opinions, issued in Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region and dated 7 June 2024, aim to support green computing industry development in the Horinger data center cluster. Section 1 provides that new large and super-large data centres (3,000 standard racks or more) should in principle be located in the Horinger cluster, and projects that do not meet the siting requirement do not receive the support policies. Section 2 covers power: coordination of computing, grid and renewable-energy planning; a green-power share of not less than 80%; long-term contracts between renewable generators and computing centres; green direct supply; and renewable quota allocation for projects with at least 10 billion yuan of fixed-asset investment and over 10,000P of computing capacity. Section 3 covers network interconnection and platform incentives: a reward of 10% of platform settlement, up to 2 million yuan per year, for firms connecting to the multi-cloud platform, and a reward of 30%, up to 2 million yuan, for buyers of at least 1 million yuan in annual compute services. Section 4 requires retirement of data centres with annual PUE above 1.5, sets new data centres at PUE 1.2 or below, and encourages low-carbon certification and standards work. Sections 5 and 6 provide a one-off 5 million yuan research grant for newly certified technology centres, talent treatment, and one-off rewards of up to 2 million yuan for projects in national data-element cases, plus pilot demonstration programmes. The text is marked as partially deleted and contains no separate enforcement provisions.

title: 个人信息保护合规审计管理办法 (Measures for the Administration of Personal Information Protection Compliance Audits)
summary_short: Sets rules for personal information protection compliance audits in China, effective 1 May 2025. Processors handling over 10 million people's data must audit at least every two years, and protection departments may order audits after serious risks or large leaks, following an annexed audit guideline.
summary_long: Order No. 18 of the Cyberspace Administration of China, adopted 20 May 2024, effective 1 May 2025. Governs personal information protection compliance audits within the PRC, defined as supervisory review of compliance with laws and administrative regulations. Processors may audit internally or through entrusted bodies (Art. 3); those handling over 10 million people's data must audit at least every two years (Art. 4). Protection departments may require an audit for serious risks or after a security incident exposing 1 million or more personal records or 100,000 or more sensitive records (Art. 5); the processor pays and must rectify and report within 15 working days (Arts. 8, 11). Processors over 1 million people must designate a protection officer, and major platforms an external-majority oversight body (Art. 12). Audit bodies must be qualified, may not subcontract, and may not audit the same object more than three consecutive times (Arts. 7, 14, 15). An annex guideline lists review items, including consent, notice, cross-border transfer, automated decisions, sensitive data and minors under 14. Violations are dealt with under the Personal Information Protection Law and the Network Data Security Regulations, with criminal liability where applicable (Art. 18). State organs and public-affairs bodies are excluded (Art. 19).

title: 个人信息出境认证办法
summary_short: Sets rules for certifying outbound transfers of personal information by Chinese personal information handlers through accredited certification bodies, with eligibility limits and an effective date of 1 January 2026.
summary_long: Issued by the CAC and SAMR (Order No. 20, 14 October 2025, adopted 21 July 2025), the measures govern transfers of personal information out of China through certification by a professional certification body. Eligible handlers must not be critical information infrastructure operators and must cumulatively transfer, from 1 January of a year, personal information (excluding sensitive personal information and important data) of 100,000 to under 1 million people, or sensitive personal information of under 10,000 people; splitting volumes to evade a security assessment is prohibited. Before applying, handlers must give notice, obtain separate consent where required and complete an impact assessment covering six listed factors. Certificates last three years, with renewal applications due six months before expiry. Certification bodies must file with the CAC, report certificate changes within five working days, and suspend or revoke certificates when transfers fall outside the certified scope. The CAC and SAMR set rules and standards, supervise certification, and may summon certified handlers facing significant risk. Overseas handlers must act through a domestic establishment or designated representative. The measures take effect on 1 January 2026.

title: 个人信息出境标准合同办法 (Measures on the Standard Contract for Outbound Transfer of Personal Information)
summary_short: Sets conditions for transferring personal information outside China by concluding the State standard contract with the overseas recipient. Requires a protection impact assessment and filing with the provincial cyberspace authority within 10 working days; bars splitting transfers to avoid security assessment. Effective 1 June 2023.
summary_long: Sets conditions for transferring personal information outside China by concluding the State standard contract with the overseas recipient. Art. 4 limits this route to non-CII processors below caps: under 1 million individuals processed, and since 1 January of the prior year under 100,000 individuals' information and under 10,000 individuals' sensitive information transferred abroad; splitting transfers to avoid a security assessment is barred. Before transfer, the processor must carry out an impact assessment (Art. 5). The contract must follow the Annex, which the regulator may adjust; the contract must take effect before transfer (Art. 6). Within 10 working days of effectiveness the processor files the contract and assessment report with the provincial cyberspace authority (Art. 7); reassessment and refiling are required on specified changes (Art. 8). Regulators must keep information confidential (Art. 9); anyone may report violations (Art. 10); regulators may interview processors facing major risk or incidents (Art. 11). Violations are handled under the PIPL, with criminal liability where applicable (Art. 12). Effective 1 June 2023; non-compliant transfers already under way must be rectified within six months (Art. 13).

title: 中华人民共和国个人信息保护法 (Personal Information Protection Law of the PRC)
summary_short: China's Personal Information Protection Law, in force from 1 November 2021. It sets rules for processing personal information of natural persons in China, including processing abroad that targets or analyses people in China. It imposes consent, notice, impact-assessment and cross-border transfer duties, individual rights, and sanctions.
summary_long: The Personal Information Protection Law applies to processing of natural persons' personal information within the PRC and, in defined cases, to processing outside the PRC that offers products or services to, or analyses or assesses the conduct of, persons in China. It sets general principles and lawful bases for processing, with consent as one basis among several. Sensitive personal information, including biometric data and information on minors under fourteen, is subject to separate rules and heightened consent requirements. State organs have special rules, including a data localisation requirement. Cross-border provision requires one of several conditions, such as a state security assessment, certification, or a standard contract, plus notice and separate consent. Individuals have rights of access, correction, deletion, portability and explanation. Processors must adopt internal management measures, appoint a personal information protection officer above a volume threshold, conduct impact assessments for specified activities, and undergo compliance audits. Large platforms have additional duties. Automated decision-making must be transparent and fair, and individuals may refuse decisions made solely by automation. Authorities may investigate, inspect and interview parties. Penalties include warnings, confiscation of unlawful gains, suspension of applications, fines up to stated amounts or a share of prior-year turnover for serious cases, and criminal or civil liability.  Article 74 sets the entry-into-force date.  Article 72 excludes purely personal or household processing.

title: 互联网平台价格行为规则
summary_short: China's Internet Platform Price Conduct Rules set price-related duties and prohibitions for platform operators and in-platform operators selling goods or services online. They apply from 10 April 2026 for a stated validity of 5 years.
summary_long: The rules govern pricing conduct by platform operators and in-platform operators that sell goods or provide services through internet platforms in mainland China. Platform operators may not restrict in-platform operators' pricing autonomy through fee increases, traffic limits, search demotion or delisting, and must publish fee standards and seek in-platform operators' opinions for at least seven days before changing fees. Sellers must display prices and fees clearly, disclose dynamic pricing and personalised pricing rules, and state the conditions of promotions and estimated prices. Operators may not sell below cost to exclude competitors, use data and algorithms to set different prices for the same transaction without consumers' knowledge, collude on prices, or spread false price-rise information. Price fraud and misleading price displays are prohibited. Consumers must be shown and able to cancel no-password payment, bundled services and automatic renewal. Platform operators must maintain a price compliance system, handle personal information lawfully and complete required algorithm filings. The Development and Reform, market regulation and cyberspace authorities supervise compliance. Minor violations that are corrected promptly and cause no harm are not administratively penalised.

title: Security Management Measures for the Application of Facial Recognition Technology
summary_short: Regulates the use of facial recognition technology to process facial information within the PRC, setting purpose, notice, consent, impact assessment, storage, minors and filing duties for processors, with supervision by cyberspace authorities. Effective 1 June 2025.
summary_long: The Measures regulate using facial recognition technology to process facial information within the PRC, excluding processing for research, development and algorithm training. Processors must have a specific purpose and sufficient necessity, and must give prior notice of listed matters. Where consent is the basis, it must be separate and voluntary, and withdrawal must be possible by convenient means; guardian consent is required for under-14s, who also need dedicated rules. Facial information is stored in recognition devices and not transmitted externally unless laws permit or separate consent is obtained, and retention is limited to the necessary minimum. A personal information protection impact assessment is required before use and again on purpose changes or major security incidents. Facial recognition may not be the sole identity verification method where alternatives exist, and misleading or coercing individuals into accepting it is prohibited. Installation in public spaces must be necessary for public security and signposted, and is barred in private areas of public places. Processors holding facial information of 100,000 individuals must file with a provincial-level or higher cyberspace administration within 30 business days. Regulators supervise and receive complaints. Violations are handled under other laws, with criminal liability where a crime is constituted. The text sets no fine amounts. Effective 1 June 2025.

title: 上海市进一步扩大人工智能应用的若干措施
summary_short: Shanghai municipal measures (issued 28 July 2025) offering subsidies, computing, model and corpus vouchers, R&D, talent and cluster support to AI firms and institutions to expand AI application.
summary_long: The measures were issued by the Shanghai Economic and Informatization Commission on 28 July 2025 and set 12 support measures to expand AI application in Shanghai. Measures 1 to 3 issue computing-power, model and corpus vouchers of 600 million, 300 million and 100 million yuan, with municipal rent subsidies of up to 30% for leased compute, up to 50% of contract value for large-model deployment, and up to 30% for purchased corpora, all capped. Measures 4 and 5 fund key technology and scientific-intelligence projects at up to 30% to 70% of approved investment, capped at 50 million yuan. Measures 6 to 8 support innovation service platforms, new R&D institutions (3 to 5 years, up to 500 million yuan), rewards for product sales or leasing, first-version software applications and demonstration scenarios. Measure 9 covers AI towns and clusters with rent reductions or one-time fees for 6 months to 3 years. Measure 10 provides talent funding and personal awards of up to 300,000 yuan. Measures 11 and 12 cover investment funds and open-source incentives of up to 5 million yuan. The text sets no prohibitions, reporting duties or penalties and works through government subsidies, with implementation left to the issuing bodies.

title: 上海市数据条例
summary_short: Shanghai municipal regulation adopted 25 Nov 2021 and in force from 1 Jan 2022. It governs data processing in Shanghai: personal information consent and rights, limits on biometric and image-capture identification, automated decision rules, public-sector data cataloguing, sharing and opening, data exchange and trading, Lingang cross-border data pilots, and data security duties.
summary_long: Regulation adopted by the Shanghai Municipal People's Congress Standing Committee on 25 November 2021, in force from 1 January 2022. It applies to data processing in Shanghai and sets general rules for data rights, circulation and security. Personal information processing requires consent, prior notice and separate consent for biometric data; individuals may request correction and deletion in listed cases; image-capture and identification devices in public places must be necessary, signposted, and may not be the sole entry verification method. Automated decisions must be transparent and fair, must not impose unreasonable price differences, and must offer a non-personalised option or easy refusal for marketing. Public-sector data must be catalogued and shared through the municipal big-data resource platform on a sharing-first basis, subject to negative lists; it is classed as unconditional, conditional or non-open for opening, and may be commercially developed by authorised operators. The regulation provides for data exchanges and trading rules, a Lingang low-risk cross-border data catalogue to be explored with reporting duties, and a catalogue of important data whose processors must appoint responsible persons and submit periodic risk assessment reports. Public bodies that breach its rules face corrective orders and disciplinary measures; public-interest lawsuits may be brought over unlawful personal information processing affecting many people. Other sanctions follow national law.

title: 上海市浦东新区促进无驾驶人智能网联汽车创新应用规定
summary_short: Pudong New Area regulation, in force 1 February 2023, governing road testing, demonstration and commercial operation of driverless intelligent connected vehicles on designated roads and areas. Enterprises must obtain safety self-declaration confirmation, plates and operating certificates, carry insurance, and meet remote-monitoring, data-reporting and accident duties.
summary_long: The regulation governs driverless intelligent connected vehicles (no driver or safety operator on board) in road sections and areas designated in Pudong New Area, covering road testing, demonstration application, demonstration operation and commercial operation under a graded, risk-based approach (Arts. 1-3, 18). Enterprises must obtain confirmation of a safety self-declaration after review by government bodies with third-party institutions and experts (Arts. 5-10), meeting requirements on legal status, remote monitoring, emergency takeover staff and insurance (Art. 6). Vehicles must meet minimal-risk and functional-safety requirements and complete staged road testing (Arts. 7-9). Confirmed vehicles obtain temporary plates (Arts. 12-13); commercial operation requires transport qualifications and operating certificates (Arts. 15-16). Enterprises must report software upgrades and faults, upload data to municipal platforms, keep fault and accident records for at least a year, meet network and data security duties, and store important data domestically (Arts. 17, 21-27). The enterprise first pays for damage attributed to the vehicle, subject to recourse (Art. 29). Non-compliance can lead to suspension, rectification or termination (Arts. 31-32); the text states no monetary fines.

title: Regulations for the Promotion of the Development of the Artificial Intelligence Industry in Shanghai Municipality
summary_short: Shanghai municipal regulation, in force from 1 October 2022, promoting the AI industry through compute and data measures, R&D and industrial support, and public-sector and sectoral application. It sets prohibitions on certain algorithmic practices for AI providers and employers, and biometric safeguards.
summary_long: The Regulations apply within the municipality's administrative region (Art. 3) and come into force on 1 October 2022 (Art. 72). They assign roles to municipal and district governments and create an AI strategy advisory committee and an AI ethics expert committee (Arts. 5-7, 66). They provide for public compute and data-opening measures, R&D and industrial support, special funds, additional deductions for AI R&D costs, and talent policies (Arts. 13-34). Application provisions cover government procurement, demonstration lists and sector uses such as manufacturing, finance, medicine and transport (Arts. 46-63). Article 65 provides checklist-style compliance review for high-risk AI products and services, disclosure in advance and after-the-fact control for lower-risk ones, and sandbox regulation. Article 67 prohibits products that endanger security or privacy, discrimination on listed grounds, and algorithmic price discrimination or consumption fraud. Article 68 requires biometric service providers to adopt secure technical safeguards, and Article 69 regulates employers' use of AI in labor discipline, scheduling and recruitment or promotion decisions. Article 67 states no penalty; Article 65 allows a list of non-administrative penalties for minor violations to be formulated.

title: 小型个人信息处理者个人信息保护简化措施规定（征求意见稿）
summary_short: Draft CAC rule, open for comment until 3 May 2026, for small personal information handlers processing fewer than 100,000 individuals' data. It simplifies notice, cross-border transfer, audit, impact assessment, breach notification and penalty mitigation duties under the PIPL; the effective date is left blank.
summary_long: The draft Provisions on Simplified Personal Information Protection Measures for Small Personal Information Handlers, published for comment by the Cyberspace Administration of China on 3 April 2026, applies within mainland China to handlers processing personal information of fewer than 100,000 individuals (Art. 2). Its stated aim is to ease Personal Information Protection Law duties for small and micro enterprises. Handlers may publish processing rules in simplified form (Art. 4), and park or property managers may publish unified rules for tenants (Art. 5). Notice of transfers on merger, split or dissolution may be given by posting or pop-up (Art. 9). Cross-border provision is exempt from security assessment, standard contract and certification in listed cases, such as contract performance, cross-border HR management, emergencies, legal duties, and cumulative transfers under 100,000 non-sensitive individuals a year (Art. 11). Compliance audits and impact assessments may use simplified forms at least every five years, with records kept (Arts. 14–15). Breach notice may be posted where direct notice is impossible (Art. 17). Certified handlers may skip audits during certification validity (Art. 18). No or reduced penalties apply in listed circumstances (Arts. 19–20). The effective date is left blank (Art. 22).

title: (Trial) Measures for Science and Technology Ethics Reviews
summary_short: China's trial Measures require science and technology ethics reviews for S&T activities involving humans, laboratory animals, or other ethically risky activities. Work units set up ethics committees, and listed high-risk activities also need expert reconsideration and registration. Effective 1 December 2023.
