Violations carry up to two years' imprisonment and/or fines up to 1 million yen (Art. 92). Provisions take effect in stages by Cabinet Order within nine months to two years of promulgation.
text_version: current consolidated text on e-Gov as of 2026-10-14 (latest revision listed: enforcement 2026-09-18, by Act No. 38 of 2026)

title: 情報処理の促進に関する法律及び特別会計に関する法律の一部を改正する法律 (Act Partially Amending the Act on Promotion of Information Processing and the Special Accounts Act, 2025)
summary_short: Amends Japan's Information Processing Promotion Act and Special Accounts Act to add designation of high-speed information processing semiconductors, public selection of operators to produce them, and state-backed bond, fund and guarantee financing for advanced semiconductor and AI-related technology, mainly for Reiwa 7 to 12 fiscal years.
summary_long: Act No. 30 of 2025 amends the Act on Promotion of Information Processing (Act No. 90 of 1970) and the Special Accounts Act. It adds a chapter under which the Minister of Economy, Trade and Industry may designate high-speed information processing semiconductors by cabinet-order category and must publish the designation. It adds a chapter on advanced semiconductor and AI-related technology in which the Minister publicly solicits and selects operators for production facilities, trial production and demand development, with plans that require submission, ministerial approval for changes, and reporting duties. The Independent Administrative Agency for Information-technology Promotion (IPA) may provide capital contributions, bond and loan guarantees and interest subsidies, and may issue bonds or borrow under ministerial approval. The government may issue bonds and provide guarantees, and the energy special account is used for these measures, with fiscal authority limits per fiscal year stated in the text. Related tax provisions reduce registration tax and adjust business tax for selected operators. Fines apply for failure to report. The Act takes effect on a date set by cabinet order within three months of promulgation, and includes a five-year review clause.

title: スマートフォンにおいて利用される特定ソフトウェアに係る競争の促進に関する法律 (Act on Promotion of Competition for Specified Smartphone Software; Act No. 58 of 2024)
summary_short: Japan's Act on Promotion of Competition for Specified Smartphone Software designates providers of smartphone basic software, app stores, browsers and search engines above size thresholds. It bars them from favouring their own offerings, misusing third-party data and unfairly treating app providers, and requires disclosure, data transfer and default-setting measures.
summary_long: The Act sets rules for designated providers of four categories of smartphone software: basic software, app stores, browsers and search engines. The Fair Trade Commission designates providers whose business scale meets a size set by cabinet order, using indicators such as user numbers, and designated providers must notify the Commission of their scale. Designated providers may not use data obtained from third-party app or website operators to compete with them, may not impose unfair terms on app providers, may not restrict alternative app stores, payment systems, browser engines or the display of offers made through external web pages, and may not favour their own services in search results. They must disclose conditions for acquiring data, allow users to have their data transferred, implement default-setting and choice-screen measures, and file annual reports. The Commission may issue recommendations and exclusion orders. Surcharges of 20% of relevant sales apply to breaches of Articles 7 and 8, rising to 30% for repeat cases. Damages liability applies without a defence of absence of fault, and criminal penalties apply to breaches of secrecy orders and final exclusion orders. The Act takes effect on a date set by cabinet order no later than 18 months after promulgation, with some provisions effective on promulgation and others six months later.
text_version: as promulgated 2024-06-19 (Act No. 58 of 2024), e-Gov text in force from 2025-12-18

title: Data Protection (General) Regulations, 2021 (Legal Notice 263 of 2021)
summary_short: Kenya's Data Protection (General) Regulations 2021 (Legal Notice 263 of 2021) are made under the Data Protection Act and set duties for data controllers and processors on consent, data subject requests, retention, processor contracts, automated decisions, impact assessments, breach notification and cross-border transfers, commenced 14 January 2022.
summary_long: Legal Notice 263 of 2021 sets detailed rules under Kenya's Data Protection Act. It was published and commenced on 14 January 2022 and is shown as revised to 31 December 2022. It applies to data controllers and data processors, except civil registration entities covered by separate regulations. Operative provisions cover consent and lawful bases; data subject requests (restriction, objection, access, rectification, portability, erasure) with fixed response periods; direct-marketing rules with an opt-out, and a fine of up to twenty thousand shillings or six months' imprisonment for unlawful commercial use; retention schedules and processor contracts; in-country storage for specified state-interest processing; data protection by design; breach notification to the Data Commissioner; transfers abroad based on safeguards, adequacy, necessity or consent; prior impact assessments for listed high-risk processing, including automated decisions and biometric data; and exemptions for national security by Cabinet Secretary certificate and for public-interest situations.

title: Data Protection (Registration of Data Controllers and Data Processors) Regulations, 2021 (Legal Notice 265 of 2021)
summary_short: Kenyan regulations under the Data Protection Act that require every data controller and data processor to register with the Data Commissioner, set application, renewal and change-notification procedures and fees, and exempt small entities that do not process Third Schedule purposes.
summary_long: The Regulations, made under section 18 of the Data Protection Act (Cap. 411C), set the procedure for registering data controllers and data processors with the Data Commissioner. Every controller and processor must register (reg. 4), and a controller is a person who determines the purpose and means of processing. Applications use Form DPR1, attach establishment documents and descriptions of purposes and data categories, and pay fees in the Second Schedule (reg. 5). The Commissioner verifies the application, issues a certificate within fourteen days, and the certificate is valid for twenty-four months (regs. 7-9). Refusals must be notified with reasons within twenty-one days, and renewal follows the same process (regs. 10-12). Entities with fewer than ten employees and turnover or revenue below KES 5 million are exempt from mandatory registration, except where they process purposes listed in the Third Schedule, and they must still comply with Parts IV and VI of the Act (reg. 13). The Office publishes a list of registered entities every thirty days, and changes must be notified within fourteen days (regs. 14-15). The Commissioner may cancel or vary certificates on listed grounds (reg. 16). Processing without registration, providing false information, and continuing processing after non-renewal are offences (reg. 18). The header gives commencement as 14 January 2022, while reg. 1(2) sets six months from publication.

title: Data Protection Act, 2019 (No. 24 of 2019)
summary_short: Kenya's Data Protection Act 2019 regulates processing of personal data by controllers and processors established in Kenya or processing data of persons located there. It creates the Data Protection Commissioner's Office and sets data subject rights, processing principles, registration, breach notification, transfer limits and penalties. Commenced 25 November 2019.
summary_long: The Act applies to processing of personal data by data controllers and processors that are established or ordinarily resident in Kenya and process in Kenya, and to those not established in Kenya that process personal data of data subjects located in Kenya (s. 4). It establishes the Office of the Data Protection Commissioner (Part II) and requires registration of controllers and processors under thresholds the Commissioner prescribes (Part III). Part IV sets processing principles, data subject rights, consent conditions, rules on children's data, a right not to be subject to solely automated decisions, impact assessments and breach notification (72 hours to the Commissioner, ss. 25-43). Sensitive and health data have further processing conditions (Part V). Transfers out of Kenya require proof of safeguards or listed grounds, and the Cabinet Secretary may require localisation for certain processing (Part VI). Exemptions cover personal, national security, journalism and research purposes (Part VII). The Commissioner handles complaints, issues enforcement and penalty notices, and may impose administrative fines up to five million shillings or, for undertakings, one per cent of turnover, whichever is lower (Part VIII). Offences carry fines and imprisonment, and a general penalty applies. Individuals may claim compensation from controllers or processors (s. 65).

title: 인공지능 발전과 신뢰 기반 조성 등에 관한 기본법 (Framework Act on the Development of Artificial Intelligence and the Creation of a Foundation for Trust; Act No. 20676)
summary_short: Framework act promoting AI development and trust in Korea. Covers AI business operators: transparency labelling, safety measures for large-compute AI, and duties for high-impact AI, plus state support and institutions. Enforcement date stated as 22 Jan 2026.
summary_long: The Framework Act on the Development of Artificial Intelligence and the Creation of a Foundation for Trust (Act No. 20676, dated 21 Jan 2025) sets basic principles and state responsibilities for AI. It establishes a National Artificial Intelligence Committee, an AI Policy Center and an AI Safety Institute, and authorizes state support for AI technology, standards, learning data, startups, clusters and data centers. It applies to AI business operators, including developers and AI-using operators, and to conduct outside the country that affects the domestic market or users. Operators must notify users when using high-impact or generative AI, and label generative outputs and realistic synthetic media. Operators of AI systems above a Presidential Decree compute standard must manage lifecycle risks and report results to the Minister. High-impact AI, defined by listed sectors and rights-affecting decisions, triggers risk management, explanation, user protection and human oversight duties; impact assessment is an endeavour obligation. Foreign operators above Presidential Decree thresholds must designate a domestic agent. Administrative fines of up to 30 million won and imprisonment of up to 3 years for disclosing committee secrets are provided; the Minister may order cessation or correction of violations.

title: 인공지능 발전과 신뢰 기반 조성 등에 관한 기본법 시행령 (Enforcement Decree of the AI Basic Act)
summary_short: Enforcement decree of South Korea's AI Basic Act. Sets the carve-out for defence and intelligence AI, criteria for high-impact and computing-scale AI systems, labelling and notice duties for AI business operators, impact assessments, record-keeping, support programmes and domestic-agent criteria. In force from 22 January 2026.
summary_long: Presidential Decree No. 36053 (enacted 21 January 2026, in force 22 January 2026; digital medical device parts from 24 January 2026) implements the AI Basic Act. It excludes AI used solely for listed defence, intelligence and security tasks designated by the Defence Minister, the National Intelligence Service director or the Police Commissioner. It sets up the National AI Strategy Committee, its support secretariat, AI policy centres, the AI Safety Research Institute and an AI industry association. For AI business operators it requires notice to users when a product or service is based on high-impact or generative AI, with labelling of generated output in human- or machine-readable form, and exemptions for obvious use or internal use. It defines a computing-scale test for AI safety duties (cumulative training compute of 10^26 floating-point operations, plus state-of-the-art technology and broad serious-risk criteria). It sets a procedure for the Ministry to confirm whether a system is high-impact, with 30-day response periods. Operators must publish risk-management information, keep records for five years and carry out impact assessments. Large operators must appoint a domestic agent under revenue, user-number and fine-history criteria. Fines follow a standards table in an annex not reproduced in this text. The decree also covers support for learning data, a data integration system, AI industrial clusters and sandbox infrastructure.</parameter>
text_version: as enacted: Presidential Decree No. 36053, 2026-01-21, in force 2026-01-22

title: 공직선거법 제82조의8 (Public Official Election Act, Art. 82-8 on deepfake election campaign videos; 2023 amendment)
summary_short: South Korea's Public Official Election Act governs presidential, National Assembly and local elections, including campaigns, polls and election media. Article 82-8 bars producing or disseminating realistic AI-generated synthetic content for campaigning from 90 days before election day through election day, and requires labelling of such content at other times.
summary_long: The Act applies to presidential, National Assembly, local council and local government head elections. It sets rules for campaigning, candidate registration, campaign materials, broadcast and online election coverage, public opinion polls and election-management bodies. Article 82-8 prohibits producing, editing, distributing, screening or posting realistic AI-generated audio, images or video for campaigning from 90 days before election day to election day, and requires a label on such material at other times. Article 110 bars false statements of fact about candidates, and Article 82-4 lets election commissions and candidates request deletion of unlawful online content. Pollsters must register, and publication of polls on party support or expected winners is barred from six days before election day. Broadcasters and internet news outlets face fairness duties, with reply rights and commission review. Penalties are cross-referenced; the penalty chapter is not in the fetched text, which is part 1 of 2.
text_version: current consolidated text in force 2026-10-02 (Act No. 22052, 2026-09-29)

title: 개인정보 보호법 (Personal Information Protection Act, as amended 2023)
summary_short: South Korea's general personal information statute. Governs collection, use, provision, cross-border transfer and security of personal data by public and private processors, and grants data-subject rights, including against fully automated decisions. In force from 11 September 2026 (Act No. 21445, amended 10 March 2026).
summary_long: South Korea's general personal information statute, as amended by Act No. 21445 (10 March 2026) and in force from 11 September 2026. It establishes the Personal Information Protection Commission (PIPC), basic plans and guidelines (Arts. 7–12). Processors, public and private, must meet rules on collection and use, purpose limits, notice, consent (with extra rules for children under 14), sensitive data, unique identifiers, CCTV, outsourcing, pseudonymised data and cross-border transfers (Arts. 15–28-11). Further duties cover security, privacy policies, privacy officers, domestic agents for foreign processors above size thresholds, file registration, certification, impact assessments and breach notification (Arts. 29–34-2). Data subjects have rights of access, portability, correction, deletion, suspension, and refusal or explanation of fully automated decisions (Arts. 35–38, 37-2). Damages, statutory damages up to KRW 3 million, dispute mediation and class actions follow (Arts. 39–57). The PIPC may order corrective measures and impose surcharges up to 3% of total revenue (10% in listed cases) (Arts. 63–64-2). Criminal penalties reach ten years' imprisonment or KRW 100 million; administrative fines reach KRW 50 million (Arts. 70–75).
text_version: current consolidated text in force 2026-09-11 (Act No. 21445, 2026-03-10)

title: 전기통신사업법 (Telecommunications Business Act; 2021 amendment, Art. 50(1)(9)–(11) on app market operators)
summary_short: Korea's Telecommunications Business Act (consolidated text; stated effective date 1 October 2026) governs telecom carriers, value-added service providers, app market operators and handset distribution, and is not AI-specific. It sets registration, foreign-ownership, merger and tariff rules, user-protection and anti-discrimination duties, app-market prohibited conduct, and penalties.
summary_long: The Telecommunications Business Act (consolidated text; stated effective date 1 October 2026) governs basic carriers, value-added service providers, app market operators and handset distribution in Korea, and is not AI-specific. Telecom and value-added providers must register or notify (Arts. 6, 22), and certain facility-based carriers face a 49% foreign-ownership cap (Art. 8), public-interest review of certain share acquisitions (Art. 10) and approval of mergers and business transfers (Art. 18). Universal service duties (Art. 4) and tariff filings for designated services (Art. 28) also apply. App market operators must protect users on payments and refunds (Art. 22-9); Art. 50(1)(9) to (11) prohibit forcing a payment method, unduly delaying app review and unduly deleting content. Handset subsidy rules (Arts. 32-11 to 32-16) bar discriminatory subsidies and require cost disclosure. Other provisions cover identity checks for contracts, content blocking for minors (Art. 32-7), removal of illegal filmed material (Art. 22-5) and caller-number spoofing (Art. 84-2). Art. 2-2 reaches conduct abroad affecting the domestic market or users. Enforcement includes corrective orders, licence revocation, surcharges up to 3% of relevant sales (Arts. 52, 53) and criminal penalties (Arts. 94-99).
text_version: current consolidated text in force 2026-10-01 (Act No. 21503, 2026-03-31)

title: Projet de loi portant mise en oeuvre de certaines dispositions du règlement (UE) 2024/1689 du Parlement européen et du Conseil du 13 juin 2024 établissant des règles harmonisées concernant l'intelligence artificielle [...] et portant modification de : 1° la loi du 1er août 2018 portant organisation de la Commission nationale pour la protection des données et du régime général sur la protection des données ; 2° la loi modifiée du 23 décembre 1998 portant création d'une commission de surveillance du secteur financier ; 3° la loi modifiée du 7 décembre 2015 sur le secteur des assurances
summary_short: Luxembourg draft law (bill 8476, deposited 23 Dec 2024, in committee) to implement certain provisions of EU Regulation 2024/1689 (AI Act) and amend the 2018 CNPD law, the 1998 CSSF law and the 2015 insurance law. Operative provisions and dates are not in the fetched page.
summary_long: The bill, filed by Elisabeth Margue on 23 December 2024 and referred to the Commission des Médias et des Communications, is titled as a law implementing certain provisions of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (the AI Act) and amending three Luxembourg laws: the law of 1 August 2018 on the organisation of the Commission nationale pour la protection des données and the general data protection regime; the amended law of 23 December 1998 creating the Commission de surveillance du secteur financier; and the amended law of 7 December 2015 on the insurance sector. The dossier page records opinions from the CSSF, the CNPD, the Conseil d'État and other bodies, the last dated 10 July 2026, and a status of 'En commission'. The fetched page contains the title and dossier metadata only, not the bill's articles, so the scope of designations, obligations, penalties and entry-into-force dates is not described here. The registry stage 'introduced' is superseded by the dossier's committee stage.

title: Mākslīgā intelekta centra likums
summary_short: Establishes the Artificial Intelligence Centre, a non-profit foundation that coordinates AI projects, gives opinions on AI and deepfake use in elections, and runs a special regulatory environment where it may grant permits to disapply certain legal requirements. Applies from 20 March 2025; some tasks from 1 June 2026.
summary_long: The law creates a non-profit foundation, the Artificial Intelligence Centre, registered under the associations and foundations law. Its tasks include promoting AI use in public and private sectors, identifying AI security risks, issuing opinions on AI or deepfake use in pre-election campaigns, election day and parliamentary appointment processes, preparing guidelines, organising datasets for AI training, and organising a special regulatory environment. The centre may run competitions, receive state budget funding, donations and other income, and process personal data for its tasks. Its structure is a council of nine members and a director appointed by the council. Under Article 8, the centre, working with competent institutions, issues administrative acts that grant permission not to apply specified legal requirements for participants. AI development in this environment may not endanger state, public, environmental or economic security, or human health and life. Sanctioned companies and entities linked to Russia or Belarus are excluded, as are companies subject to criminal sanctions in the past five years. Administrative acts can be appealed in court. Article 9 allows the centre to request personal data from national state information systems for AI development, limited to data minimisation, pseudonymisation where possible, named participants and deletion after development. Transitional provisions set the foundation's registration deadline at 31 March 2025 and start the election-opinion task from 1 June 2026. The text includes a 2026 amendment to Article 8 effective 1 June 2026.</parameter>

title: Grozījumi Tiesībsarga likumā (2026. gada 15. janvāra likums)
summary_short: Amends the Latvian Ombudsman Act so that the Ombudsman may request and access documentation of artificial intelligence systems needed in a case, and may ask the market surveillance authority to test an AI system with technical means if that documentation is insufficient. In force from 11 February 2026.
summary_long: The amending act changes the Latvian Ombudsman Act (Tiesībsarga likums). It adds two powers to Article 13: to request and access the documentation of artificial intelligence systems needed in a review case (point 15), and to ask the market surveillance authority, within its competence, to organise testing of an AI system with technical means where that documentation is insufficient (point 16). Article 27(1) is rewritten so that when the Ombudsman requests information under points 1, 1.1, 5, 13, 15 and 16 of Article 13, it sets the scope of that information and a reasonable time limit for providing it. The act also amends the informatory list of EU directives, removing points 1 and 4 and adding four directives on equal treatment, web and mobile accessibility, and work-life balance. The text sets no penalties, defines no AI system and specifies no numeric thresholds. The Saeima adopted it on 15 January 2026, the President promulgated it on 28 January 2026, and the publication metadata gives entry into force on 11 February 2026.

title: Data Protection Act 2017 (Act No. 20 of 2017)
summary_short: The Data Protection Act 2017 regulates the processing of personal data by controllers and processors in Mauritius. It requires registration, lawful processing, security measures, breach notification, impact assessments and prior consultation, restricts transfers abroad, and grants data subject rights. The Data Protection Commissioner enforces it. Commencement is by proclamation, with w.e.f. 15 January 2018 stated in the text.
summary_long: The Act establishes the Data Protection Office, headed by a Data Protection Commissioner, with powers to investigate complaints, require information, seek preservation orders, issue enforcement notices, audit controllers and processors, and issue codes and guidelines. Controllers and processors must register with the Commissioner before acting as such, and certificates are valid for 3 years. Controllers must apply principles on purpose limitation, accuracy and storage limitation, and must keep records of processing and designate a data protection officer. Processing requires consent or another listed lawful basis, and special categories of personal data face further restrictions. Processing data of a child below 16 requires parental or guardian consent. Personal data breaches must be notified to the Commissioner within 72 hours where feasible, and to data subjects when high risk applies. Impact assessments are required for high-risk processing, including automated evaluation with legal or significant effects. Prior authorisation or consultation applies in listed cases. Transfers outside Mauritius require safeguards or another listed basis. Data subjects have rights of access, rectification, erasure, objection and not to be subject to solely automated decisions. Offences carry fines and imprisonment, with amounts varying by provision. The Act also applies to controllers not established in Mauritius that use equipment in Mauritius, and they must nominate a representative. It repeals the earlier Data Protection Act and contains transitional provisions.},

title: Resolución que modifica las Disposiciones de carácter general aplicables a las instituciones de crédito (biométricos) (DOF 01-07-2026)
summary_short: Amends Mexico's CNBV general provisions for credit institutions to permit facial biometric identity verification alongside fingerprints, checked against official registries, and sets technical and security requirements for biometric databases (Annex 71). Applies from the day after DOF publication.
summary_long: CNBV resolution dated 25 June 2026 amending Articles 51 Bis, 51 Bis 2, 51 Bis 3, 51 Bis 4 and 51 Bis 5 of the general provisions for credit institutions and replacing Annex 71. Credit institutions must verify, for in-person operations, that the biometric data of the person presenting an identity document matches official registries, with a 90% match for fingerprints and an online check of facial biometrics added. Institutions may build their own biometric databases in place of certain requirements, subject to matching against official registries, notice to the Commission within 20 business days, annual validation of security mechanisms, and deletion of data when use stops. Biometric data may not be sold, transferred, shared or interoperated with other institutions or third parties for identity checks. The Commission may request information and, after a hearing, order partial or total suspension of a database for serious or repeated non-compliance. The Commission may also authorise alternative processes and documents. Annex 71 sets capture requirements and security controls such as segregation, encryption and penetration testing. Institutions must comply within 90 business days of entry into force, the day after DOF publication.

title: Acuerdo por el que la Comisión Nacional de Energía expide el modelo de contrato para la interconexión, conexión o ambas a la Red Nacional de Transmisión o a las Redes Generales de Distribución para Centrales Eléctricas, Sistemas de Almacenamiento de Energía Eléctrica y Centros de Carga (DOF 17-03-2026)
summary_short: Mexico's Comisión Nacional de Energía issues a model contract for interconnecting or connecting power plants, storage systems and load centers to the national transmission or general distribution networks, signed by CFE and the applicant. It takes effect the business day after DOF publication and repeals four earlier CRE instruments.
summary_long: The Comisión Nacional de Energía (CNE) issues a model contract for interconnecting, connecting or both power plants, storage systems and load centers to the Red Nacional de Transmisión or the Redes Generales de Distribución. It covers generation and storage permit holders, load centers, and self-consumer or qualified users, with a 1 MW contracted-load threshold for load centers on distribution networks (Art. 2). Contracts are signed by CFE as transmitter or distributor and the applicant, on CENACE instruction, and set out measurement systems, maintenance, guarantees, works, term, termination, force majeure and dispute resolution through the Market Rules. Performance under the contract may be suspended in emergencies (Cl. Vigésima Segunda) and, when measurement systems cannot be reviewed, a fixed monthly payment applies as a penalty (Cl. Vigésima Séptima). Modifications that change the model require prior CNE approval; other addenda do not. Generation under 0.7 MW in Generación Distribuida is excluded from this model. The agreement enters into force the business day after DOF publication and repeals four earlier CRE instruments.

title: Acuerdo de la Comisión Nacional de Energía por el que se emiten las Disposiciones Administrativas de Carácter General para regular la figura de Autoconsumo de Energía Eléctrica (DOF 12-12-2025)
summary_short: Mexican electricity regulator's rules on self-consumption (Autoconsumo) of electricity: generation permits, isolated and interconnected schemes, surplus-sale terms, market operation and a self-consumption registry. Binding on permit holders, users, grid operators and market participants from the business day after DOF publication.
summary_long: Administrative rules issued by Mexico's Comisión Nacional de Energía, signed 28 November 2025, implementing the self-consumption (Autoconsumo) figure of the Electricity Sector Law and its regulation. They apply nationwide to permit holders, self-consumption users, grid operators, CENACE, the state supply company and market participants. Chapters II to IV set rules for isolated and interconnected self-consumption, with or without surplus sales, including grid studies, connection contracts, reverse-power protection and storage backup for intermittent generation. Community micro-grids of 0.7 to 5 MW are covered. Chapter V sets minimum contract contents between permit holders and users. Chapter VI governs wholesale market representation and surplus-sale payments, calculated from the levelised cost of the last long-term auction and the local marginal price. Chapter VII requires a Self-Consumption Registry, updated within 15 business days of changes or by 31 March each year. Permits end if users' maximum demand stays below 50% (conventional) or 30% (renewable) of installed capacity for twelve months. Transitional provisions cover existing isolated permits and interim market representation; annexes contain a model surplus-sale contract and the registry form. Infringements are sanctioned under the Electricity Sector Law.

title: Acuerdo de la Comisión Nacional de Energía por el que se establecen los requisitos para obtener el permiso de generación para autoconsumo interconectado en centrales eléctricas cuya capacidad sea entre 0.7 y 20 megawatts (MW) (DOF 06-08-2025)
summary_short: Mexican energy regulator CNE agreement (dated 23 July 2025) setting the documents applicants must file to obtain a generation permit for interconnected self-supply plants of 0.7 to 20 MW. Applicants must submit the listed items to the CNE; the CNE will resolve requests under implementing regulations.
summary_long: The Agreement of the Comisión Nacional de Energía (CNE), dated 23 July 2025, sets the requirements for a generation permit for interconnected self-supply (autoconsumo interconectado) in power plants with capacity between 0.7 and 20 MW, following a simplified procedure referred to in the Electric Sector Law. Applicants must file with the CNE an authorised form and documents, including identification and legal capacity, technology and capacity, a georeferenced site proposal, a simplified single-line diagram, a simplified works schedule, a business plan if the plant is not yet installed, evidence of technical and financial capacity, a shareholding diagram where applicable, and proof of fee payment. Documents already held by the CNE or in the citizen digital file need not be resubmitted. The CNE must analyse and resolve requests under the regulation and administrative provisions to be issued. Transitional provisions make the Agreement effective when the implementing regulations of the Electric Sector and Energy Planning and Transition laws enter into force; the CNE must publish the form on its website and in the Diario Oficial de la Federación, review it annually, and register the procedure in the citizen portal. Permit holders must observe the contract models, calculation methodologies and criteria for consideration that the CNE issues. No penalties are set out in the text.

title: Decreto por el que se reforman, adicionan y derogan diversas disposiciones de la Constitución Política de los Estados Unidos Mexicanos, en materia de simplificación orgánica (DOF 20-12-2024)
summary_short: Decree reforming, adding and repealing provisions of the Mexican Constitution to simplify public bodies. It extinguishes autonomous agencies including the Federal Competition Commission and the Federal Telecommunications Institute, moves competition and telecom regulation to the Executive, and reassigns data-protection oversight. In force the day after DOF publication.
summary_long: The decree reforms, adds and repeals provisions of Articles 3, 6, 26, 27, 28, 41, 76, 78, 89, 105, 113, 116, 123 and 134 of the Mexican Constitution. Article 6 A II sends competence over personal data held by private parties to the law under Article 90, and Article 6 A VIII subjects obligated bodies to a general transparency and data-protection law. Article 28 assigns telecommunications and broadcasting regulation and competition enforcement to the Executive, acting through its ministry and a competition authority. Article 134 requires public entities to eliminate duplicated functions and structures. Congress has ninety natural days from entry into force to adapt the relevant laws. The Federal Competition Commission and the Federal Telecommunications Institute are extinguished when the reformed Article 28 paragraphs take effect, 180 days after the secondary competition and telecommunications laws enter into force (Transitorio Décimo and Décimo Primero); other listed bodies, including the National Institute for Transparency, Access to Information and Personal Data Protection, the Energy Regulatory Commission and the National Hydrocarbons Commission, are extinguished when the secondary access-to-information law takes effect. Acts and contracts of extinguished bodies stay valid, and their staff's labour rights are preserved. The decree takes effect the day after DOF publication.

title: Acuerdo mediante el cual el Pleno de la Comisión Reguladora de Telecomunicaciones aprueba y emite los Lineamientos para la Identificación de Líneas Telefónicas Móviles (DOF 09-12-2025)
summary_short: Obliges mobile telephony concessionaires and resellers in Mexico to link every mobile line to a holder verified with an official ID, in person or remotely; lines not linked after a transitional period are disabled, except for emergency calls. Takes effect on publication.
summary_long: Administrative rule of Mexico's CRT under the telecommunications law, binding on mobile concessionaires and resellers. Title I defines terms and requires every mobile line to be linked to a holder to be enabled. Title II sets identity validation: natural persons present an official ID checked against government sources; foreigners a passport or temporary CURP; legal persons and public entities corporate and authority documents. Linking is in person or remote, the remote route with a liveness test and up to three attempts. Article 10 caps natural persons at ten linked lines. Title III requires management and consultation platforms and bars storing biometric data or ID copies; failures must be reported to the CRT. Title IV sets personal-data security and confidentiality duties. Title V gives the CRT verification powers. Transitional provisions set 30- and 60-day deadlines for the platforms, a 30-day window to start linking, disabling of lines still unlinked 120 business days after the platform deadline, and a postpaid exemption for holders of ten or more lines. Non-compliance is sanctioned under the Ley.

title: Dictamen de la Comisión de Igualdad de Género, con proyecto de decreto por el que se adiciona un quinto párrafo al artículo 20 Quáter a la Ley General de Acceso de las Mujeres a una Vida Libre de Violencia
summary_short: Committee report proposing a fifth paragraph to Art. 20 Quáter of Mexico's General Law on Women's Access to a Life Free of Violence. If enacted, it would sanction non-consensual technological generation or dissemination of intimate sexual images, videos or audio simulating sexual acts of a person.
summary_long: Committee report (dictamen dated 21 October 2025, published in the Gaceta Parlamentaria on 17 February 2026) approving with modifications an initiative to amend the Ley General de Acceso de las Mujeres a una Vida Libre de Violencia. Its single operative article (Único) adds a fifth paragraph to Art. 20 Quáter. The paragraph would sanction any intentional conduct consisting of the total or partial generation, by technological means, of intimate sexual images, videos or audio that simulate sexual acts or pornographic representations of a person, without that person's consent, approval or authorization. It would also sanction the disclosure, distribution, publication or sharing of such material, even if created wholly or partly by those means. No penalty is specified in the text. The comparison table records 'Se mantiene texto vigente' (current text retained) for the proposed Art. 5 definition of generative artificial intelligence and for proposed Art. 20 Septies; the operative decree does not amend either. The decree enters into force the day after publication in the Diario Oficial de la Federación. The file is pending, with the legislative deadline extended to 31 August 2027.
text_version: Committee dictamen (Comisión de Igualdad de Género, 21 Oct 2025) with proyecto de decreto, Gaceta Parlamentaria 17-02-2026 Anexo IV pp. 133-144

title: Iniciativa con proyecto de decreto Que reforma y adiciona diversas disposiciones del Código Penal Federal y de la Ley Federal de Derecho de Autor, en materia de inteligencia artificial generativa
summary_short: Bill adding to the Federal Criminal Code definitions of generative AI tools and a misuse offence (6 months to 4 years' prison, 100 to 600 days' fine), and amending the Federal Copyright Law on AI-assisted works. Introduced 30 April 2025; would apply from the day after publication.
summary_long: Bill presented to the Chamber of Deputies on 30 April 2025 by PAN deputies, referred to joint committees on Justice and Science and Technology. It would add to the Federal Criminal Code a definition of generative AI tools (high autonomy, content such as text, images, audio, video or code created from deep learning models in response to commands) and an offence of their misuse: deceptive non-consensual manipulation of images or recordings passed as real; tools fed with non-selectively extracted facial or private data, unlawful remote biometric identification, or falsification of official documents; dissemination of confidential information or illegally obtained images; and generating works presented as one's own for commercial registration, infringing protected works or constituting fraud. Such conduct would carry six months to four years' imprisonment and 100 to 600 days' fine. The Federal Copyright Law would classify works by the technology used, exclude from protection autonomously generated AI content that infringes existing rights, lacks authorization for its inputs and does not disclose sources, technology or authors, and extend the computer-program definition to AI-assisted systems. Entry into force the day after publication in the Diario Oficial de la Federación. The text names no enforcement authority.

title: Decreto por el que se expide la Ley General de Aguas y, se reforman, adicionan y derogan diversas disposiciones de la Ley de Aguas Nacionales (DOF 11-12-2025)
summary_short: Mexico's Ley General de Aguas sets out the human right to water for personal and domestic use, allocates federal, state and municipal responsibilities, and reforms the Ley de Aguas Nacionales on concessions, assignments, the water registry, rainwater harvesting, reuse and penalties. In force the day after DOF publication.
summary_long: The decree enacts the Ley General de Aguas and amends, adds to and repeals provisions of the Ley de Aguas Nacionales. The General Law recognizes the human right to water for personal and domestic use and its interdependence with other rights, sets principles and elements of the right (including accessibility, affordability and quality), and allocates powers among the Federation, states and municipalities. It establishes a National Water Strategy with baseline scenarios and goals fixed at ten, twenty, forty and sixty years, regulates rainwater harvesting and community and municipal water systems, and provides for water-operating bodies and a water culture program. The amendments to the Ley de Aguas Nacionales revise rules on concessions and assignments, reallocation of volumes, the National Public Water Registry, discharge permits, irrigation districts and water reuse. They set administrative fines in Unidades de Medida y Actualización, revocation and suspension of titles, and prison terms and fines for offences against national waters. Transitional provisions set 180-day periods for state harmonization and for regulations, and the decree enters into force the day after its publication in the Diario Oficial de la Federación.

title: Decreto por el que se reforman, adicionan y derogan diversas disposiciones de la Ley Federal de Competencia Económica y de la Ley Federal de las Entidades Paraestatales (DOF 16-07-2025)
summary_short: Mexico's Federal Economic Competition Law (text consolidated to the reforms of 16-07-2025 and 14-11-2025) prohibits monopolistic practices, illicit concentrations and barriers to competition, requires prior authorization of large mergers, and empowers the Comisión Nacional Antimonopolio to investigate and fine firms. It contains no AI-specific provisions.
summary_long: The Ley Federal de Competencia Económica, a general competition statute published 23 May 2014 and consolidated to the reforms of 16-07-2025 and 14-11-2025, applies to all economic agents and activity nationwide. It defines key terms, including the Agencia de Transformación Digital y Telecomunicaciones, and creates the Comisión Nacional Antimonopolio, a decentralised body governed by a five-member Pleno with an Autoridad Investigadora. The Comisión may order removal of barriers to competition, regulate access to essential inputs, and determine substantial market power, including designating Agentes Económicos Preponderantes in broadcasting and telecommunications. Book Two prohibits absolute monopolistic practices, which are null by law, and relative practices, and sets rules on relevant markets and illicit concentrations. Book Three governs investigations, trial-type procedures, interim measures, and merger control: concentrations above UMA-denominated thresholds need prior authorisation, with review periods, conditions and exemptions, plus leniency and formal opinions. Title VII sets fines expressed in UMA or as percentages of revenue, disqualification of individuals, and divestiture. The provided text reproduces Articles 1 to 131; later provisions, including Article 134 on damages, appear only in the outline. It contains no AI-specific provisions.

title: Ley Federal de Protección de Datos Personales en Posesión de los Particulares (DOF 20-03-2025)
summary_short: Mexico's private-sector data protection law. Private controllers and processors must observe principles, obtain consent, issue privacy notices, secure data and honour ARCO rights. Supervised by the Secretaría Anticorrupción y Buen Gobierno, with sanctions and crimes. In force from the day after its DOF publication of 20 March 2025.
summary_long: Mexico's private-sector data protection law governs personal data processing by private natural and legal persons nationwide (Arts. 1, 2). It excludes credit reporting companies and purely personal, non-commercial collection (Art. 1). Controllers must follow principles of lawfulness, purpose, consent, proportionality and accountability, with express consent for financial and sensitive data (Arts. 5-13). They must issue privacy notices, keep security measures, report significant breaches and designate a person to handle requests (Arts. 14-19, 29). Data subjects hold ARCO rights, including objection to solely automated processing that significantly affects them (Arts. 21-26). Transfers, domestic or foreign, are governed by Arts. 35-36; binding self-regulation schemes are permitted (Art. 37). The Secretaría Anticorrupción y Buen Gobierno supervises compliance and resolves rights-protection and verification procedures (Arts. 38-57). Fines range from 100 to 320,000 times the UMA, with an additional fine for repeated breaches and up to doubling for sensitive data (Art. 59). Imprisonment of three months to five years applies to specified data-misuse offences (Arts. 62-64); civil damages claims are preserved (Arts. 53, 61). Transitory provisions move the former INAI's data protection functions to the Secretaría.

title: Decreto por el que se reforman y adicionan diversas disposiciones de la Ley Federal del Trabajo y de la Ley Federal del Derecho de Autor, en materia de derechos de las personas trabajadoras artistas intérpretes o ejecutantes (DOF 14-05-2026)
summary_short: Mexico's consolidated Federal Copyright Law (last reformed DOF 14-05-2026) sets authors', performers', producers', broadcasters' and publishers' rights, exceptions, collective management, registration, arbitration, and administrative and criminal sanctions. Its 2026 amendments require consent or written agreement for AI-generated clones or imitations of performers' voice or image.
summary_long: The instrument is the consolidated Federal Copyright Law (Ley Federal del Derecho de Autor) of Mexico, published in the Diario Oficial on 24 December 1996 and reformed through 14 May 2026. Titles I to III set moral and economic rights of authors and rules for transferring and licensing them, including contracts for publishing, music, performance, broadcasting, audiovisual and advertising works. Titles IV and V cover protection of computer programs, databases, performers, phonogram and videogram producers and broadcasters. Title VI lists exceptions and limitations, and Titles VII and VIII cover folk-culture expressions and the copyright and rights-reserve registries. Title IX regulates collective management societies, which need prior authorization from the Instituto Nacional del Derecho de Autor. Title XI covers civil actions, precautionary measures and arbitration. Title XII sets administrative fines in units of measurement and actualization and commercial fines in minimum-wage days, and includes notice-and-takedown rules for online service providers. The 2026 amendments state that AI-generated results are covered by performers' image and voice protection (Art. 87), that AI programs are protected like literary works (Art. 102), and that AI-based voice or image cloning requires prior written agreement (Arts. 118 VII and 121). The transitional provisions repeal the 1956 law and set a 90-day period before the 1996 law entered into force.

title: Decreto por el que se adicionan diversas disposiciones de la Ley Federal del Trabajo, en materia de Plataformas Digitales (DOF 24-12-2024)
summary_short: Mexico's consolidated Federal Labor Law (text as of 14-05-2026) sets general rules for employment relationships, working hours, wages, rest, profit sharing, dismissal and special worker categories, applying throughout the Republic. Provisions added by DOF 24-12-2024 cover digital platform workers, including limits on reinstatement and severance (Arts. 49, 50, 127).
summary_long: The Ley Federal del Trabajo, in its consolidated text as of 14-05-2026, applies throughout the Republic to employment relations under Article 123(A) of the Constitution. It defines workers, employers and employment relationships, regulates probation, training and fixed-term contracts, and prohibits subcontracting of personnel except for registered specialised services. It sets maximum working hours, overtime limits, rest days, paid vacations, minimum and other wages, wage protections, and worker profit sharing. It governs suspension and termination of employment, reinstatement and compensation, and imposes employer duties on workplace safety, electronic recording of working hours (Art. 132 XXXIV), protocols against discrimination and harassment, and training. Special chapters cover women (maternity protections), minors (minimum age 15, prohibited hazardous work), trust workers, ship and aircraft crews, and other categories. Penalties for certain procedural misconduct are fixed at 100 to 1000 times the Unidad de Medida y Actualización (Art. 48). Provisions added by DOF 24-12-2024 cover digital platform workers: no mandatory reinstatement except for collective-rights violations (Art. 49 VI), a three-month severance plus twenty days' salary per year of service (Art. 50 IV), and profit sharing above 288 hours worked per year (Art. 127 IX). The platform chapter itself (Arts. 291-A et seq.) is outside the fetched part.

title: Decreto por el que se reforman, adicionan y derogan diversas disposiciones de la Ley General en Materia de Desaparición Forzada de Personas, Desaparición Cometida por Particulares y del Sistema Nacional de Búsqueda de Personas, así como de la Ley General de Población (DOF 16-07-2025)
summary_short: Mexico's General Population Law as amended on 16 July 2025: makes the national identity key (CURP) a mandatory universal identity document that may include biometric data, requires public and private entities to request it for procedures, and sets fines for non-compliance with biometric integration duties.
summary_long: Consolidated text of the Ley General de Población, last reformed DOF 16-07-2025. The 2025 decree adds Arts. 91 Bis to 91 Sexies and 114 Bis. Art. 91 Bis makes the Clave Única de Registro de Población (CURP) a mandatory national identity document, universally accepted, that may also contain fingerprints and a photograph, in physical and digital form. The Secretaría de Gobernación must integrate biometric data into the CURP by transfer from authorities of the three levels of government or by attendance at enabling centres, and integration requires the holders' prior consent. Art. 91 Ter links the biometric CURP to the National Health System Registry. Art. 91 Quater creates a single identity platform within the National Population Registry. Art. 91 Quinquies assigns the digital CURP to the Agencia de Transformación Digital y Telecomunicaciones. Art. 91 Sexies requires use of the CURP for digital identity validation and obliges all public and private entities to request it for their procedures and services. Art. 114 Bis sets fines of 10,000 to 20,000 times the daily Unidad de Medida y Actualización for authorities and private parties that repeatedly fail to meet Art. 91 Bis duties, after prior warning. Transitory provisions set 90-day and 120-day deadlines for the platform, consent mechanisms, the CURP requirement and a biometric programme for children and adolescents.

title: Ley en Materia de Telecomunicaciones y Radiodifusión (DOF 16-07-2025)
summary_short: Mexican federal statute on telecommunications, broadcasting and satellite services, published in the DOF on 16 July 2025. It creates the regulatory framework for the Comisión and Agencia, spectrum and concession regimes, interconnection and asymmetric rules for dominant or substantially powerful operators, and repeals the Federal Telecommunications and Broadcasting Law. It is not AI-specific.
summary_long: Federal statute published in the DOF on 16 July 2025 that issues the Ley en Materia de Telecomunicaciones y Radiodifusión and repeals the Federal Telecommunications and Broadcasting Law. The text is not AI-specific. It declares telecommunications and broadcasting public services of general interest and bans discrimination in their provision (Art. 2), and places spectrum and orbital resources in the public domain (Art. 32). The Comisión Reguladora de Telecomunicaciones, a desconcentrated body of the Agencia de Transformación Digital y Telecomunicaciones, regulates the sectors, sets general rules and may impose sanctions (Arts. 7–10); its five-member Pleno decides listed matters (Art. 12). Title Three sets concession regimes: a single concession for convergent services and spectrum or orbital concessions granted by tender or direct award, with transfer, shareholding notice and extension rules (Arts. 45–101). Title Four covers networks and services: interconnection, number portability, infrastructure sharing, obligations of preponderant or substantially powerful economic agents (Art. 123), network neutrality (Arts. 131–132), public property for deployment and satellite communication. Per the outline, Title Five covers authorizations and Title Six the Public Telecommunications Registry (Arts. 159–181). Title Seven is not described in the outline. The provided excerpt contains the full text of Arts. 1–140; entry-into-force terms are not stated in it.

title: Ley del Sector Eléctrico (DOF 18-03-2025)
summary_short: Mexican statute (DOF 18 March 2025) governing the electricity sector: national grid planning and control, generation and supply permits, transmission and distribution, retail supply and the wholesale market run by CENACE. Federal jurisdiction. Contains no AI-specific provisions.
summary_long: Ley del Sector Electrico, published in the Diario Oficial de la Federacion on 18 March 2025. This record covers part 1 of 2: Articles 1 to 175 and the Chapter X heading; the remaining text is not in this document. The law regulates planning and control of the Sistema Electrico Nacional, and generation, including permits for plants of 0.7 MW or more, distributed generation, self-consumption, cogeneration, long-term production and mixed investment schemes. It sets rules for transmission and distribution, including interconnection, metering and suspension of service, and for commercialization, including basic supply and last-resort supply. It also covers qualified users, small systems, storage, electromobility, rights of way and land negotiations, local content, and a wholesale market operated by CENACE, with market rules, CNE monitoring and a universal energy service fund. Further provisions cover consultation with indigenous and Afro-Mexican communities, social impact assessments, clean energy certificates, tariff methodologies, standards and reliability measures. Administrative sanctions are referred to the law in Article 106, but penalty amounts are not set out in this part. Federal jurisdiction applies. No AI-specific provisions appear.

title: Ley del Sistema Nacional de Investigación e Inteligencia en Materia de Seguridad Pública (DOF 16-07-2025)
summary_short: Establishes Mexico's Sistema Nacional de Investigación e Inteligencia en Materia de Seguridad Pública: a CNI-operated Plataforma Central de Inteligencia interconnecting public security databases and, under conditions, other records, with AI tools permitted in analysis. Binding nationwide; in force the day after DOF publication, 16 July 2025.
summary_long: The Law creates the Sistema Nacional de Investigación e Inteligencia en Materia de Seguridad Pública, coordinated by the Secretaría de Seguridad y Protección Ciudadana and operated by the Centro Nacional de Inteligencia (CNI). The Consejo Nacional, chaired by the federal Executive, may issue agreements of mandatory observance for all Mexican authorities. The CNI runs the Plataforma Central de Inteligencia, to be connected in real time to listed public security systems and, on request or by agreement, to other public bodies, certain private persons and foreign entities. Private holders of relevant databases must collaborate in their transmission, consultation and supply; private entities may only grant the CNI access to specified systems under an agreement. Intelligence processing may use automation and artificial intelligence tools. Information must be encrypted and access controlled by user levels; personnel must be certified and subject to trust controls. Unauthorized disclosure of confidential information is punishable under administrative and criminal legislation. Data handling must follow federal transparency and personal data laws. The Platform must begin full operation within 180 working days of entry into force.

title: Decreto por el que se otorgan estímulos fiscales para apoyar la estrategia nacional denominada "Plan México", para fomentar nuevas inversiones, que incentiven programas de capacitación dual e impulsen la innovación (DOF 21-01-2025)
summary_short: Mexican presidential decree of 20 January 2025 granting federal income-tax incentives under the Plan México strategy: immediate deduction of new fixed-asset investment and an additional deduction for training and innovation spending, for taxpayers meeting listed requirements, in force the day after DOF publication and running to 30 September 2030.
summary_long: Presidential decree of 20 January 2025 granting federal income-tax incentives under the Plan México strategy. Article Primero grants them to legal entities and individuals meeting listed requirements, including a positive tax-compliance opinion, an investment project, an SEP dual-education agreement where relevant, and a compliance certificate from an Evaluation Committee. It allows immediate deduction of new fixed-asset investments acquired until 30 September 2030, subject to a two-year minimum use period and exclusions; Article Segundo sets deduction percentages by asset type and activity for 2025-2026 and 2027-2030. Article Cuarto grants an additional deduction of 25% of the increase in training spending for active workers and of innovation spending linked to patent or initial-certification projects. Article Quinto creates the Evaluation Committee (chaired by SHCP) and caps total incentives at 30 billion pesos, of which 28.5 billion for investment and 1.5 billion for the additional deduction, with at least 1 billion for taxpayers with prior-year income up to 100 million pesos. Article Sexto excludes listed taxpayers; Article Séptimo requires repayment of tax, adjustments and surcharges on non-compliance; Article Octavo authorises SAT rules. Entry into force is the day after DOF publication; the decree repeals the 2023 export-sector incentive decree.

title: Decreto por el que se otorgan estímulos fiscales en los Polos de Desarrollo Económico para el Bienestar (DOF 22-05-2025)
summary_short: Federal tax decree granting incentives to taxpayers that start operations and carry out productive activities inside Polos de Desarrollo Económico para el Bienestar: immediate 100% deduction for new fixed assets and additional 25% deduction for training or innovation spending, fiscal years 2025–2030. Effective on DOF publication.
summary_long: Federal tax decree granting incentives for taxpayers that start operations and carry out productive activities inside Polos de Desarrollo Económico para el Bienestar, for fiscal years 2025 to 2030. Taxpayers resident in Mexico (and non-residents with a permanent establishment) and developers authorised by a state entity may apply an immediate 100% deduction for new fixed assets used in a pole (Art. Tercero), and an additional 25% deduction for increases in training or innovation spending (Art. Cuarto). Eligibility requires tax compliance and a fiscal domicile in the pole; the training incentive also requires a dual-education programme with the Secretaría de Educación Pública, and taxpayers subject to certain tax-authority presumptions are excluded (Art. Segundo, Séptimo). The Secretaría de Economía declares each pole on the collegiate opinion of an inter-ministerial committee, which the decree creates with guideline-making powers (Art. Primero, Décimo). The SAT issues general rules (Art. Décimo Tercero). The decree sets no penalties; non-compliance means losing the incentives and paying tax, indexation and surcharges. The text has no AI-specific provisions; employment_labor is assigned because the vocabulary has no tax-incentive domain.

title: Decreto por el que se adicionan diversas disposiciones al Reglamento de la Ley Federal del Derecho de Autor (DOF 24-09-2026)
summary_short: Adds Chapter V to the Reglamento de la Ley Federal del Derecho de Autor (arts. 37 Bis to 37 Nonies) on technological protection measures, rights management information, and online service providers' notice-and-takedown procedures. Signed 28 August 2026; enters into force 90 business days after publication in the DOF.
summary_long: The decree adds Chapter V to Title IV of the Reglamento de la Ley Federal del Derecho de Autor. Article 37 Bis makes protection of technological protection measures and rights management information independent of copyright protection, and excludes circumvention where the related content is not protected under the Ley. Article 37 Ter defines 'material' and 'contenido' by reference to protected works, performances, phonograms, broadcasts and artists' images and voices. Articles 37 Quáter and 37 Septies list required contents of notices and counter-notices, including sworn statements and acknowledgment of the sanction under Article 232 Quinquies of the Ley. Article 37 Quinquies bars online service providers from conditioning the removal step on registration certificates or other documentation, except for counter-notices. Article 37 Sexies requires providers to make a notice form available to users. Article 37 Octies requires providers to notify the original notifier of a counter-notice. Article 37 Nonies sets restoration of disputed content within 10 to 15 business days where requirements are met, and requires removal again if the original notifier shows a proceeding was started within 15 business days. Transitional provisions apply prior rules to notices filed before entry into force and provide that implementation costs are borne by existing budgets.</parameter>

title: Reglamento de la Ley del Sector Eléctrico (DOF 03-10-2025)
summary_short: Implementing regulation of Mexico's Ley del Sector Eléctrico, published in the DOF on 3 October 2025. It sets rules for electricity planning, permits, grid access, tariffs, user complaints, storage, clean-energy certificates and social impact authorizations for federal energy authorities and sector participants.
summary_long: Implementing regulation of Mexico's Ley del Sector Eléctrico, published in the DOF on 3 October 2025. Título Primero sets planning duties, standards and permits for generation, storage and trade, with a 60-working-day decision period and a five-year bar after revocation. Título Segundo covers energy justice, electrification and the Fondo de Servicio Universal Energético. Título Tercero regulates distributed generation, self-consumption, wholesale-market generation and mixed-development schemes. Título Cuarto covers transmission and distribution, grid access, connection contributions, metering reviews (back-billing up to ten years), complaints, maximum regulated tariffs and 48-hour outage notice. Título Quinto covers qualified users, small systems and micro-grids, market rules, clean-energy certificates, storage, electromobility and related permits. Título Sexto requires social impact authorizations before construction, with prior indigenous consultation. Penalties are largely referred to the Ley and the Ley Federal de Procedimiento Administrativo; the text provided is part 1 of 2, running to Art. 217.

title: Acuerdo por el que se modifica el diverso que establece los bienes de uso dual, software y tecnologías cuya exportación está sujeta a regulación por parte de la Secretaría de Economía (DOF 03-07-2026)
summary_short: Amends Mexico's 2020 dual-use export control agreement by adding Articles XXVIII-XXX. Federal agencies must keep export controls compatible with Wassenaar, Australia Group, NSG and MTCR lists, and Mexico must update its annexes and adopt US additional controls on notification. In force the day after DOF publication.
summary_long: The instrument amends the Secretaría de Economía agreement published in the Diario Oficial de la Federación on 27 December 2020, which sets the tariff fractions of dual-use goods, software and technologies whose export is subject to Secretaría de Economía regulation, by adding Articles XXVIII, XXIX and XXX. Article XXVIII requires the federal public administration bodies and entities to ensure that Mexico's controls are compatible with the control lists of the Wassenaar Arrangement, the Australia Group, the Nuclear Suppliers Group and the Missile Technology Control Regime. Article XXIX requires Mexico to modify annexes I to VI of the agreement to be consistent with those agreed controls. Article XXX requires Mexico to update the agreement in a timely manner to adopt and maintain additional export controls in force in the United States, based on a written notification from that country. The operative provisions set no penalties or individual enforcement measures. The instrument enters into force the day after its publication in the Diario Oficial de la Federación. The recitals state that the Wassenaar Arrangement allows high-technology firms access to previously restricted inputs and production lines.

title: Acuerdo por el que se emiten los Lineamientos para la implementación de la Ventanilla Única de Autoconsumo para la atención prioritaria, expedita y simultánea de trámites asociados a la generación de energía eléctrica bajo la figura de Autoconsumo (DOF 08-05-2026)
summary_short: Secretaría de Energía rule, signed 4 May 2026, setting a unified expedited procedure through the Ventanilla Única de Autoconsumo for permits, studies, interconnection and surplus-sale contracts for self-consumption generation of 0.7 to 20 MW, isolated or interconnected. Binding from the business day after publication.
summary_long: Secretaría de Energía rules, signed 4 May 2026, establishing a priority, expedited and simultaneous procedure, run through the Ventanilla Única de Autoconsumo (VUA) module of the Ventanilla Energía platform, for procedures tied to self-consumption generation plants of 0.7 to 20 MW, isolated or interconnected. The procedures cover a MISSE (social impact statement) authorization by SENER, which isolated self-consumption up to 20 MW is exempt from; generation permits by the CNE; CENACE studies, admission and Registro de Activos Físicos; and CFE interconnection, service and surplus-sale contracts. Each authority has fixed working-day deadlines for admission, decisions and contract signing, for example 30 working days for a CNE permit decision after admission. Applicants who miss a deadline or receive a negative decision may continue through the Ordinary Route. Transitional provisions let pending requests move to these rules, and CFE must register the related procedures on the citizen portal within 30 working days of entry into force. The rules enter into force the business day after publication.

title: Acuerdo número 09/09/26 para garantizar los derechos de niñas, niños, adolescentes y jóvenes en la interacción, uso responsable y seguro de los dispositivos digitales personales, así como de tecnologías de aprendizaje en las escuelas públicas y particulares del Sistema Educativo Nacional (DOF 22-09-2026)
summary_short: SEP Acuerdo 09/09/26 sets rules for students' use of personal digital devices and learning technologies in public and private schools of the National Education System. It restricts device use during the school day in preschool, primary and secondary levels, with listed exceptions. Enters into force 3 November 2026.
summary_long: The Acuerdo 09/09/26 of the Secretaría de Educación Pública sets conditions and practices for the use of personal digital devices and learning technologies in public and private schools of the National Education System. For preschool, primary and secondary levels (Art. 2) it restricts use of mobile phones and smart devices throughout the school day, allowing use only for programmed educational purposes under teacher guidance and for personal emergencies, disability, accessibility, inclusion, health needs or extraordinary community needs. For upper-secondary schools (Art. 3) it encourages responsible use and limits non-pedagogical use during the school day, through a school assembly and four listed modalities: classroom storage, limited times and spaces, no use, and scheduled use. For higher education (Art. 4) it encourages responsible and safe use according to community agreements. State education authorities must adopt the necessary measures and may adjust them, and must review implementation every semester with the SEP (Arts. 2-4, 6). Within 180 natural days after entry into force, state authorities must issue or harmonize legal instruments (Transitorio Tercero). Annexes 1-3 contain decálogos described as guidance proposals (Art. 7). The text sets no penalties.

title: Reforma al artículo 185 Bis C del Código Penal para el Estado de Sinaloa (manipulación de contenido íntimo sexual mediante inteligencia artificial)
summary_short: Decree 699 adds two paragraphs to Article 185 Bis C of the Sinaloa Penal Code. Criminalises using AI to manipulate intimate sexual images, audio or video to create false facts appearing real and disseminate them without consent, with the penalties of the second paragraph. In force the day after publication.
summary_long: Decree 699 of the Sinaloa State Congress adds a fifth and sixth paragraph to Article 185 Bis C of the Sinaloa Penal Code, renumbering later paragraphs. The fifth paragraph applies the same penalties as the second paragraph to anyone who, using artificial intelligence, manipulates intimate sexual images, audio or video of a person to create false facts with apparent reality, in order to expose, distribute, disseminate, transmit, sell, offer or share them through print, email, telephone messages, social networks or other technological means, without the person's express, voluntary, genuine and desired consent. The sixth paragraph defines artificial intelligence as applications, programs or technology that analyse photographs, audio or video and offer automatic adjustments to alter or modify them. The text states no penalty amounts; it refers to the penalties of the second paragraph of the same article. Transitory articles set entry into force on the day after publication in the Periódico Oficial 'El Estado de Sinaloa' and repeal provisions that conflict with the decree. The masthead shows publication on 12 February 2024.
text_version: Decreto Número 699, Periódico Oficial 'El Estado de Sinaloa' No. 019, 12 Feb 2024 (pp. 3-6)

title: Guidelines for Corporate Renewable Energy Supply Scheme (CRESS), Energy Commission (Suruhanjaya Tenaga)
summary_short: Malaysian Energy Commission guidelines, issued under section 50C of the Electricity Supply Act 1990, setting rules for the Corporate Renewable Energy Supply Scheme (CRESS). They let Green Consumers buy electricity directly from renewable energy developers over the Peninsular Malaysia network, with applications opening from 30 September 2024.
summary_long: The Guidelines, issued by the Energy Commission under section 50C of the Electricity Supply Act 1990, set the procedure and conditions for the Corporate Renewable Energy Supply Scheme (CRESS) in Peninsular Malaysia. Under the CRESS, a Renewable Energy Developer (RED) owns and operates a Green Energy Plant (GEP) that supplies a Green Consumer through Open Access to the grid, with the Electricity Utility Company (EUC) acting as supplier of last resort. Participants must register under the New Enhanced Dispatch Arrangement, sign several contracts, and meet requirements including at least 51% local ownership, a GEP of at least 30MW with Direct Connection, and, where firm output is not provided, an energy storage system of at least 50% of registered capacity for four hours or a higher System Access Charge. The System Access Charge is fixed for three-year regulatory periods with a maximum variation of 15%, and excess energy may be sold to the system at 8 sen/kWh. The Commission reserves the right to revoke participant registration for construction delays or non-compliance. The text states no penalty amounts. Applications start from 30 September 2024.

title: Johor water tariff schedule including Data Centre category (Ranhill SAJ, gazetted tariff effective 1 August 2025)
summary_short: Sets Ranhill SAJ water tariff rates in RM per cubic metre and minimum charges by type of use in Johor, including a Data Centre category at RM 5.33 per cubic metre with a RM 53.30 monthly minimum. No effective date appears in the text; registry metadata gives 1 August 2025.
summary_long: The page presents a water tariff schedule from Ranhill SAJ with rates in RM per cubic metre and monthly minimum charges for six types of use. Domestic rates rise across three volume bands (0-20 m³, 21-35 m³, over 35 m³) at RM 1.05, 2.35 and 3.50, with a monthly minimum of RM 10.50. Religious institutions and welfare-approved users pay an average rate of RM 1.65 and Domestic Bulk users RM 2.75, with monthly minimums of RM 16.50 and RM 27.50. Non Domestic rates are RM 4.15 (0-35 m³) and RM 5.30 (over 35 m³) with a RM 41.50 minimum. Shipping pays an average RM 8.03 with a RM 80.30 minimum. The Data Centre category pays an average RM 5.33 per cubic metre with a RM 53.30 monthly minimum. The text states no legal basis, effective date, penalties or enforcement provisions; the effective date of 1 August 2025 comes from registry metadata only.

title: Online Safety Act 2025 (Act 866)
summary_short: Malaysia's Online Safety Act 2025 requires licensed applications and content applications service providers to mitigate exposure to harmful content, protect child users, offer reporting mechanisms and submit Online Safety Plans, enforced by the Communications and Multimedia Commission. It applies from a date set by ministerial notification.
summary_long: The Act covers applications services, content applications services and network services using internet access, excluding private messaging features, and reaches licensees outside Malaysia that provide such services in Malaysia. It creates an Online Safety Committee to advise the Communications and Multimedia Commission and an Online Safety Appeal Tribunal. Licensed applications and content applications service providers must implement code-specified measures against exposure to harmful content, issue user guidelines, provide user tools and reporting mechanisms, protect child users, make priority harmful content inaccessible, and prepare an Online Safety Plan. The Commission may issue written instructions, directions and notices of non-compliance; financial penalties for non-compliance with duties may not exceed RM10 million, and failing to comply with a written instruction or direction carries a fine of up to RM1 million plus daily fines. Secrecy breaches carry up to three months' imprisonment. The First Schedule lists harmful content categories and the Second Schedule defines priority harmful content. Commencement is set by ministerial notification.

title: Personal Data Protection (Amendment) Act 2024 (Act A1727)
summary_short: Amends the Personal Data Protection Act 2010 (Act 709) to rename “data user” as “data controller”, add data processor, data protection officer, breach notification, data portability and cross-border transfer rules, with commencement by ministerial notification in the Gazette.
summary_long: The Act amends the Personal Data Protection Act 2010 (Act 709). It replaces “data user” with “data controller” throughout, adds “biometric data” and “personal data breach” to the definitions and makes biometric data sensitive personal data. Data processors must comply with the Security Principle, and the penalty for breaching section 5(1) rises to one million ringgit, imprisonment up to three years, or both. Data controllers must appoint data protection officers and notify the Commissioner of appointments (new section 12A). They must notify the Commissioner of personal data breaches as soon as practicable, and affected data subjects where significant harm is likely (new section 12B); breach of the Commissioner-notification duty is an offence with a fine up to 250,000 ringgit, imprisonment up to two years, or both. New section 43a gives data subjects a portability right, subject to technical feasibility and data-format compatibility. Section 129 is amended so that a data controller may transfer personal data abroad, deleting the Minister's power to specify destinations. Commencement is by ministerial notification in the Gazette, with different dates possible for different provisions. Existing Commissioner orders and codes and pending proceedings are saved.

title: Regulatory framework for Internet messaging and social media service providers (ASP(C) licensing; deemed registration effective 1 January 2026)
summary_short: Declaration No. 87 of 2025 dispenses with the registration formality for internet messaging and social media service providers under the Applications Service Provider class licence, deeming them registered from 1 January 2026. Declaration No. 88 of 2025 sets standard licence conditions for class licensees.
summary_long: Declaration No. 87 of 2025, made under sections 13, 44, 46A and 126 of the Communications and Multimedia Act 1998, dispenses with the formality of registration for the class of persons providing Internet Messaging Services and Social Media Services under the Applications Service Provider Class Licence. Persons operating under the class licence are deemed registered as at 1 January 2026, and persons still registered under it become deemed licensees upon expiry of their registration. The declaration does not apply to persons exempted under paragraphs 5(e) and (f) of the Exemption Order 2000. The companion Declaration No. 88 of 2025 makes standard licence conditions in its Annex A binding on persons registered as class licensees: compliance with written laws, subsidiary legislation and consumer codes; an indemnity to the Minister and the Commission; and, for foreign licensees, a local representative who serves as point of contact, accepts legal notices and assists with directions, including on removal or blocking of content, and who must be kept available at all times. Changes to the local representative must be notified immediately.
text_version: as made 15 Dec 2025, in operation 1 Jan 2026

title: Nigeria Data Protection Act General Application and Implementation Directive (GAID) 2025
summary_short: Binding implementing directive of the Nigeria Data Protection Commission under the NDP Act 2023.
